Approved campaign map dated October 15, 2026. Shows Crown banners, the expanded walls, the restored South Ward (former Slums), the restored approach around Blackstone Temple, Maren Isle and the established city landmarks. This is the approved current geography; the PNG master remains archived unmodified in the NCFA Library.

entries.name: Map: Ledger House (Approved DM Map)
entries: {@link Open the approved Ledger House map|https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sefjoe/no-cause-for-alarm-5etools/main/img/dm/ledger_house.webp}

The existing approved Ledger House map is reused without edits from the Chapter 2 'Maps' gallery. This is the DM reference for Brakkus's inn, Session 4 dinner, Jord's lodging request, Bishop Brann's payment visit, and Tulcornix's intended late arrival. Do not replace it with an improvised or regenerated plan. The actual party location and player choices determine which entrances or rooms are used.

entries.name: Session 4 DM Run Card — Royal Takeover
entries: Start inside Kellan's Well, during the party's short rest following the fight, with Noren Vale and his Warrior Veteran alive and bound. The party's Well mission is complete; the original sluice restoration objective was explicitly removed. They have not decided either prisoner's fate. The party was underground only a few hours. The Crown prepared its takeover in advance; new flags, orders, and officers can appear fast, but the rebuilt walls, neighborhoods and streets shown on the approved map existed or were underway before they entered.

Resolve Noren: killed or handed to the watch means out of the campaign; release means he withdraws underground with the Iron Covenant organization still operating, not instant loyal allies. The Veteran is a separate decision. The current roster was Noren plus ONE Warrior Veteran, no Toughs or reinforcements.

If searched: Noren's monster gear specifies a scimitar, light crossbow and studded leather armor; his 1/day smoke bomb ability is not automatically recovered as a sellable item. Veteran's listed equipment includes greatsword and crossbow. Do not invent a secret coin pouch. Recoverable Well treasure is 375 gp in fixed locations (25 gp courier, 150 gp barracks, 75 gp salvage valuables, 125 gp command strongbox), three potions and the Decanter of Endless Water. Do not assume they collected every item; player inventory and previous actions determine actual holdings.

Let shopping double as political investigation. The gate, notices, market, and four established shops have bounded answers in Appendix J. Koven House is Crown headquarters and has a public registry. Don't force a separate exposition scene or a mandatory royal audience.

Ledger House: Brakkus offers dinner and genuine conversation with the PCs. Jord independently seeks a room because his hotel has been turned into royal guard barracks. Bishop Brann seeks Brakkus with Kellan's Well money entrusted by the departing Council: 300 gp total, 100 gp each to Jarrock, Aaron, Arunem; Pepper 0 gp because her first sentenced mission was unpaid. Record actual receipt. This is separate from the earlier Blackstone reliquary payment and anything looted at the Well.

SESSION 4 ENDING (locked): Tulcornix Avemvir comes looking specifically for Pepper, knows she killed Kaleb, and confronts her with her brother's death and the plea to save Elowen. His arrival and accusation are the LAST scene of the session. Deliver his established line and the essential fact that Elowen is held at Cardon Weavehouse, then END THE SESSION. Do not continue into bargaining with Tulcornix, the worksite, the rescue, or any other scene after his arrival. The player's response and rescue planning begin next session. If the party relocated, use credible information to bring him to Pepper; no impossible tracking.

3.5-hour flexible target: prisoners 10–25 min, gates/streets 15–25, shops/inquiries 30–75, Brakkus dinner and arrivals of Jord/Brann 40–75, then a brief Tulcornix arrival/confrontation (3–8 min) as the closing beat. Spend the session time on everything BEFORE Tulcornix, not on an Elowen rescue afterward. Follow player choices rather than filling time with another encounter.

At session end record decisions, goods actually acquired and sold, prisoner disposition, recipient of each 100 gp payment, shops visited, and what the party knows of Tulcornix/Elowen. Do NOT record a decided response to his request unless a player happened to declare it before the fade-out; their decisions are normally for Session 5.

CONTINUITY CORRECTION: During actual play only three Scouts were in the Bow Gallery, the alarm was not raised, and the prior sluice repair objective was removed. Do not present a fourth Scout, a missing waterworks repair, or withheld payment as an unfinished part of Session 3.

Shopping resale rule: the 2024 PHB sells usable mundane equipment at half its listed cost and trade valuables at full face value; Appendix J now includes fast prices. The 75 gp fixed salvage valuables in the Well's 375 gp total are already valued and must not be counted twice.

If shopping, government inquiry or an unrelated detour consumes most of the evening, Brakkus/Jord/Brann still pursue their independent Ledger House business without a staged encounter for absent PCs. Keep Tulcornix's confrontation as the final scene, and move any unfinished dinner or money handoff to a later visit instead of bending geography.

Koven House attack contingency: six total Guard stat blocks (2 entrance, 2 lobby, 2 landing) plus one Warrior Veteran sergeant inside the temporary headquarters, with two civilian clerks. Follow real alarm and travel time; barracks soldiers are NOT immediate reinforcements. The Crown responds to an actual attack as a new offense. If the party's arrest, death, or hiding makes Tulcornix's planned appearance implausible, let that outcome stand rather than teleporting him.

KOVEN HOUSE PLAYTEST MAP OVERRIDE: The existing DM key has no reliably marked upper landing; guard posts are courtyard area 1 (2 Guards), registry/main room 6 (2 Guards and two Commoner clerks), side duty room 11 (Veteran), records corridor 20/24 (2 Guards). Guards rally at doors rather than trickle into the party's attacks. Winning beats the finite local force; outside response requires physically transmitted alarm and travel.

SUPERSEDED CROSS-REFERENCES: The old Chapter 5 note that Pepper's four Council missions automatically transferred to the Crown was wrong and is corrected; Chapter 6 controls. Appendix B's former guarantee of Koven House uncommon magic treasure also referred to the unplayed criminal adventure and is superseded. A victory at the new royal headquarters earns only what is physically found and consequences of the attack.
{@b Recommended level:} 4. The return from Kellan's Well is a roleplay-led session. No encounter is scheduled; no automatic level advancement is attached to the old Koven House criminal-network plan.

entries.name: Start in the Well: Noren and His Veteran
entries: ACTUAL SESSION OPENING: The characters are in the waterworks taking a short rest AFTER capturing/binding Noren and his sole Warrior Veteran. The old sluice objective was removed and is not outstanding. The party is free to discuss the captives, inventory finds, and leave when they choose. Three Bow Gallery Scouts were encountered; no fourth NPC should appear to patch the old planned roster.

Start this week's session INSIDE Kellan's Well, not with a transition to Bellweather. Noren, the leader of the Iron Covenant, and his Warrior Veteran remain alive and bound. Their fate is not decided. Let the party search, talk, and decide without a scripted outcome.
Kill Noren: Noren is permanently out of the campaign. Handle the veteran's fate as the players actually decide. Do not immediately introduce a replacement Noren or contrive an escape.

Turn Noren over to city watch: the city gate watch accepts securely bound prisoners with the party's report that they were captured occupying Kellan's Well. The old municipal watch is undergoing a Crown transition but can still take custody without any royal petition. Noren is permanently removed from the campaign. He is not later freed or returned as an antagonist. The veteran can be turned over as well.

Release Noren: he withdraws from public view, continues managing the Iron Covenant's criminal network underground, and can become useful to the resistance to royal rule later. He is not instantly a loyal ally and does not announce a rebellion. Any choice made separately for the veteran still matters.

Noren can bargain and warn them about the Crown, which he already disclosed last session, but he is bound and has no automatic escape. Allow 10–25 minutes for this opening (or more if the players invest in it). They then leave the Well by their own route and choose what to do in Bellweather. No forced travel montage or Council summons.

On searching their possessions, use the established creature gear, any seized weapons, and Chapter 5's fixed treasure; don't double-count valuables or invent new prisoner's treasure. If the watch accepts prisoners, the captured arms are recorded based on what the PCs actually surrender.

entries.name: Chapter Overview
entries: {@b Premise.} The adventurers left a free Bellweather and return to a city transferred to the Crown. Noren warned them at the Well; now the city itself verifies his warning.

{@b Goal.} Give the party time to react to how the city has changed. Reveal consequences and competing opinions through people, public notices, employment, ordinary routines, and player-selected destinations—not a fixed string of official speeches.

{@b What is settled.} The Council negotiated the sale before the party departed and finalized it while the party was away. Koven House now serves the Crown. Bishop Brann stayed. Brakkus and Ledger House remain independent.
{@b No required battle.} Violence is possible if player choices and the other characters' decisions warrant it; there is no placed combat encounter or mandatory initiative.
{@b Tone.} The royals' authority is comically excessive, while the people enforcing, resisting, exploiting, or surviving it take their own circumstances seriously.

{@b Ending.} Tulcornix Avemvir's arrival, direct confrontation with Pepper, and revelation that Elowen is being held at Cardon Weavehouse close Session 4. The session ends there. The party decides how to respond and whether to investigate or rescue her in Session 5. Earlier Session 4 choices about shopping, prisoners, the Crown, and Ledger House remain open.

{@b Four people, one personal focus.} Brakkus, Jord and Bishop Brann have distinct reasons to remain active after the takeover. Brakkus's conversation involves the whole party. Tulcornix's arrival is guaranteed. Pepper's unresolved service is background pressure, not the plot of the evening.

entries.name: House Stucky — Crown Authority and Public Announcement
entries: King Hendrix Stucky is the reigning monarch in the distant capital, and Prince Reginald's father. Dangerous and competent, he is not planned to appear personally in the campaign. His government has broader affairs than Bellweather; do not write a compulsory king encounter.

Prince Reginald Stucky, Hendrix's son, governs Bellweather for his father. He is pompous, petty, theatrically entitled and comically evil, but soldiers and administrators can execute real orders effectively.
Princess Narcissa Stucky is Reginald's WIFE, not his sister. She rules alongside him in Bellweather; vain, privileged, casually cruel, and utterly certain of her entitlement.

The former Council arranged to transfer Bellweather before the party entered the Well. The Council members obtained money, land in another area and ducal titles in exchange. The Crown prepared troops, clerks, flags and municipal paperwork beforehand. The transfer became publicly effective while the party was underground for only a few hours. The party did not cause the sale; it happened independently of them.

PUBLIC PROCLAMATION (readable on gate and municipal postings): 'BY ORDER OF THE CROWN. The former Free City of Bellweather is henceforth governed by Their Royal Highnesses Prince Reginald Stucky and Princess Narcissa Stucky, acting in the name of His Majesty King Hendrix Stucky. Municipal offices and records are transferred to the Crown. Petitions concerning public contracts and civic records shall be submitted at the registry in Koven House. Notices shall be displayed at a height befitting royal dignity.' This is a display instruction, not a mandatory quest.

Ordinary public answers: Reginald and Narcissa govern for King Hendrix; Koven House is royal headquarters; the Council has left. The city changed flags and command structure within hours, not its architecture. Citizens may have heard rumors that the Council got money, estates and titles, but only records/credible officials can confirm precise terms. The guard includes old watchmen operating under new authority and new royal personnel.

No single public NPC knows all royal plans. Merchants disagree about the takeover. The Crown's administration is imposing new paperwork and a municipal recovery assessment, but ordinary people are still learning which old documents are valid.

entries.name: At the Table: Immediate Changes
entries: Choose concrete details appropriate to the time that has passed: new banners on familiar buildings; clerks copying records; workers paid to change signs; merchants revising prices; ordinary residents wondering whether old promises still hold. Do not present every change as a fight or a clue.

A royal proclamation can display absurd entitlement while remaining legally consequential. Write any specific tax, decree, punishment, or royal title to match decisions made at the table; no unapproved invented statute is canon yet.

The takeover began before the party arrived back in town. Background jobs, family obligations and unrelated disputes continue. Not every citizen agrees the change is bad, and not every Crown employee is malicious.

Ready city detail: workers remove a FREE CITY OF BELLWEATHER sign and install the Crown's insignia; they squabble over who gets to keep the old brass lettering. At the gates the same watchmen now carry newly stamped Crown papers. A royal clerk insists a proclamation must be hung at a height suited to a monarch looking down from horseback. These are visible facts, not required quests.

An ordinary merchant complains about replacement trade permits; a laborer appreciates finally being paid for a repair; a former Council clerk worries about losing a livelihood. Citizens can disagree without becoming automatic loyalists or rebels.

Players asking merchants what happened is expected. Appendix J includes direct observations, rumors, attitudes, and plausible answers. Their shopping trip may be the entire first half of the royal-takeover revelation.

entries.name: Open Locations and People
entries: {@b Ledger House.} Brakkus may be angry or concerned about the transfer, but he is not a quest dispenser or a mouthpiece for every NPC. Ledger House remains independent and the players can talk, rest, argue, or ignore politics.

{@b Koven House.} Now a Crown headquarters rather than the criminal hideout described in the obsolete draft. Visitors may seek appointments, information, redress, favors, or documents. No forced infiltration and no mandatory arrest. An attack contingency with actual local defenders, alerts, and consequences is specified separately under 'If They Attack Koven House — Finite Royal Defense'.

{@b Markets, taverns, workers' streets.} Show people adapting. Some prosper, some lose jobs or rights, some are mostly interested in groceries, family, pay, or a missing shipment. Let the party decide which conversations matter.

{@b Former Council staff.} Those left behind may disagree about the deal, worry about their futures, or know procedures the party can question. Do not imply the old Council still commissions official missions.
{@b Bishop Brann.} He remained in Bellweather. His views follow his religious and civic duties; they are not automatically the same as Brakkus's or the Crown's.

Cardon Weavehouse: the Crown has commandeered a street-facing textile work annex at the edge of the larger, disputed property. Kaleb's wife, Elowen, is indentured here. This does not mean the Crown controls the entire Weavehouse, Perrin Cardon arranged the servitude, or the old unplayed Chapter 8 armed occupation has already been resolved. The annex can be visited without entering the entire compound.

entries.name: If They Attack Koven House — Finite Royal Defense
entries: {@b Trigger and stakes.} This is NOT a scheduled combat; use it only if the PCs assault the guards, threaten an officer in a way that actually provokes force, or attempt an armed breach. The ground-floor registry remains accessible to peaceful visitors. No arbitrary royal audience, preemptive arrest of Pepper for the old Council sentence, or compulsory encounter.

{@b Exact finite local roster and existing DM map.} Six {@creature Guard|XMM} plus ONE {@creature Warrior Veteran|XMM} (sergeant) are on duty in the house when the party first arrives. Koven House's existing DM key is a single plan with numbered rooms, and DOES NOT identify a guaranteed stairway or second-floor landing. Use its current geometry without inventing an upper floor: 2 sentries in the outer approach/courtyard (map area 1), 2 Guards at the public entrance to the central hall/registry (map area 6), the Veteran initially in an adjoining duty room (suggest room 11), and 2 Guards protecting the inner records corridor (use west hall areas 20/24, repositioned as doors permit). Two {@creature Commoner|XMM} clerks work in the area 6 registry; they are not defenders. Room labels here represent occupation of existing rooms by the Crown, not a reimported criminal-room key. Do not add an unseen guard on every door. Guard roster is seven armed people TOTAL, even if the PCs enter by a different route.

{@b Quick stats.} Guard AC 16, HP 11, Spear +3 to hit, 4 piercing average on hit. Warrior Veteran AC 17, HP 65, two Greatsword attacks +5 to hit for 10 slashing average each; Parry reaction +2 to own AC versus one melee attack. Use the corresponding 2024 monster stat blocks in 5etools for full rules. Never add a special bodyguard reaction.

{@b Alarm, coordination, and arrivals.} The entrance sentries attempt to withdraw and call warning if they survive; they need not stand and die. Shouts can be heard according to distance, doors and noise. A surviving clerk or guard can physically flee to a watch post or send a runner: follow real movement and allow the PCs to prevent that if they can. The two hall Guards will not automatically run out to be killed one pair at a time; on hearing an attack they can withdraw into a defended threshold at area 6 and hold the route into the records wing. The Veteran moves from adjoining area 11 according to initiative and actual map distance; the last two Guards hold the west records corridor at areas 20/24 until ordered back or driven out. The initial two sentries may be dropped before warning anyone, but bystanders or clerks may still see or hear events. Give the party the physical advantage of a successful quiet attack, not a supernatural silent alarm or invisible response. Never specify arrival by round without checking map movement.

{@b Reinforcements outside this encounter.} Soldiers from the hotel being used as barracks and city-watch patrols exist, but none are a fresh wave that instantly appears in the registry. The local garrison is six Guards and one Veteran; defeated defenders stay defeated. If a witness or runner gets away, outside help can be dispatched, taking several minutes or longer depending on messenger and responder travel. For a deliberate prolonged siege, specify an actual identified patrol and its route before resolving its arrival, then apply ordinary movement. If the party defeats all seven and escapes within rounds, no replacement guards pop up just to block them.

{@b Royal defenders behave as a unit.} The two exterior Guards observe, challenge, and warn; if outmatched they fall back and shout. The two registry Guards protect the two clerks, keep doors between the party and the records wing, and fight from cover or a doorway. The Veteran makes a coordinated stand while ordering the two inner Guards to secure records or retreat. They do NOT voluntarily enter the courtyard in pairs to feed the characters seven isolated fights. If several defenders fall, the others may withdraw, barricade, yield, or escape; a guaranteed last stand or heroic suicide is not their goal. Clerks flee through actual doors if possible, or shelter under desks.

{@b What the PCs accomplish if they win.} Killing or disabling the entrance sentries means they control the doorstep, not the whole government. Defeating all six Guards and the Veteran leaves the building unprotected LOCALLY until an off-site alarm can bring help; the party can enter, flee, search or barricade it, depending on their actions and time. They can inspect public proclamations and the current registry in area 6, and may find transferred Council land grants / title documents among the more secured records in areas 20/24, confirming that Council members received money, land and ducal rank. Exact private documents require time and access but not an arbitrary skill roll if physically found; searching while under attack has normal consequences. The Crown's treasure vault, the king and the royal couple are NOT automatically present. Surrender/subdual results in custody for the new attack, not retroactive automatic enforcement of Pepper's old Council sentence. If the characters flee, witness accounts and actual injuries govern later pursuit.

{@b Political and social consequences.} An attack on the headquarters is an actual provocation: the Crown can identify suspects from witnesses, issue orders to investigate or arrest, increase physical security, and respond in proportion to injuries and deaths. An insult or public complaint alone isn't assault. Shopkeepers and the old city watch aren't instant loyal royal enforcers, but witnesses may report events. Brakkus does not become an unquestioning accomplice or omniscient pursuer; his reaction follows what he actually learns.

{@b Session 4 ending under player-caused upheaval.} Tulcornix still seeks Pepper specifically. If she evades pursuit, he can approach her through credible sightings, including at Ledger House if she returns, and his confrontation ends Session 4. If she is in royal custody or missing, DO NOT teleport Tulcornix into a secure prison or force a guard to grant access simply to hit the planned cliffhanger. Record the conflict, end at an earned stopping point, and use his confrontation when he can realistically reach her. This contingency supersedes the planned guaranteed closing scene only where player actions genuinely make that scene implausible.

{@b Guard morale and attack distinction.} For a threat or shove, first establish whether force truly begins; don't roll initiative over mere insults. If players use nonlethal melee attacks, apply 2024 rules and record living captives accordingly; lethal spell attacks and dead guards cause materially different public consequences.

{@b Royal couple's location for this immediate playtest.} Reginald and Narcissa are the Crown's announced rulers but are not physically waiting behind Koven House's newly occupied offices during the party's first Session 4 visit. Their household/court establishment is still in progress during the first hours of control. The local sergeant and clerks cannot magically bring the prince and princess into an encounter. This establishes no permanent absence from Bellweather and no future immunity from player inquiry.

{@b Combat reality check.} Six Guards have 66 total HP, the Veteran 65 (131 combined before surrender/escape). The first two guards have only 22 HP combined and can be defeated in one party turn. Against the full group, a Light cleric's burst damage, Rogue Sneak Attack, Aaron's ranged/warlock tools and Arunem's melee pressure may take down several defenders before they retaliate. Conversely the Veteran's two attacks can threaten an already injured level-4 character. Check the party's actual remaining slots, Channel Divinity, HP, short-rest recoveries and rage before judging the difficulty: the full garrison is not necessarily six simultaneous opponents. Don't buff the garrison after the PCs exploit its staggered response.

{@b If the party downs the Veteran but fails to hold the building.} A defeated or wounded sergeant can be restrained, questioned, healed, or let go according to the PCs' choices and remaining staff's actions. He is a serving officer without special knowledge of the Council's private bargain beyond what reached his desk. No automatic death saves, teleport escape, or 'named boss' rescue is scripted. If interrogated, he can identify his own orders and who signed the local notice, but he cannot summon Reginald on demand.

{@b Aftermath if the party wins and searches.} Accessible evidence includes copies of the Stucky proclamation, newly signed guard billets, municipal title transfers, and an index referencing the former Council's rewards in money, outside land, and ducal honors. A search of secured records can confirm the substance of the bargain without a treasure chest or magical secret. A clerk or guardsman escaping through a real exit can carry identifying details to another guard post in minutes, not rounds. If the party kills all defenders, uninterrupted search time remains limited by when offsite reports could plausibly arrive.

entries.name: Session Anchors: Brakkus, Jord, Bishop Brann, and Tulcornix
entries: {@b Where the guests go, regardless of PC route.} Brakkus remains at Ledger House and offers dinner when the party returns; Jord comes to seek lodgings; Bishop Brann comes to speak with Brakkus and deliver the three adventurers' 100 gp shares. These events happen independently even if the PCs spend the whole evening elsewhere. Don't relocate or teleport Jord and Brann just to force their speeches: if the party does not return, their lodging/payment encounter can be discovered on the next visit. Tulcornix, who is actively seeking Pepper, is the only personal confrontation GUARANTEED to find its subject and end Session 4. His pursuit still follows plausible witness information.

entries.name: Brakkus: Dinner and the People Behind the Adventures
entries: Brakkus sits the group down at Ledger House, with food and a genuine opportunity to talk. He realizes he knows what the party has done in Bellweather but not much about where they came from or what they want. This is the session's principal planned conversation, not a recruiting speech or an interrogation.

Suggested opening, in Brakkus's voice: 'I know what you've done around this city. I know a little about how you fight. But I don't know much about who you were before you walked through my door. So tell me about yourselves.'

Possible follow-ups, chosen naturally rather than administered in order: Where were you before Bellweather? Who or what brought you here? Is anybody elsewhere looking for you? What would you do if you could leave tomorrow? What is important to you beyond the next job?

Give Jarrock, Aaron, Arunem and Pepper space to volunteer or withhold their own histories, ask each other questions, and ask Brakkus about his past. He is a retired paladin and proprietor of Ledger House, not an omniscient investigator. Do not demand a backstory reveal from a reluctant player.
Brakkus will not become the party's commander, a substitute Council, or the default leader of an uprising; he cares first about the people under his roof.

Brakkus's detailed established past already exists in Appendix C and his NPC entry: his mother Elena, father Korgak, Ironfang Clan, mentor Vance Halford, oath to Torm, and sword The Appendix. Answer personal questions from that history; don't invent a new life story or make PC backstory revelations a mandatory sequence.

If the party never returns to Ledger House this evening, Brakkus does not summon or forcibly detain them. The planned dinner conversation remains available upon their next visit. Treat the advertised 3.5 hours as a target, not a reason to push them into the building.

entries.name: Jord: A Merchant Facing a New Administration
entries: Jord is the road-worn gnome merchant already established in the Slums aftermath, whose missing strongbox helped bring the group into that district. He has current business to attend to; he is not another person summoned just to give Pepper advice.

Jord sees that the Crown is busy processing old contracts, trading privileges, new taxes and ownership records. How those changes affect his livelihood is independent of Pepper and may open a merchant-focused conversation or future contacts.

If Pepper's status comes up, Jord offers practical advice rather than legal certainty: 'They've got a whole city of paperwork to sort through. Four jobs owed to a Council that's gone? I wouldn't go reminding them.' He does not claim the sentence has been canceled.

Jord independently comes to Ledger House looking for a room: the hotel where he was staying has been commandeered for royal guard barracks. His immediate stake is having somewhere to sleep and handle his trading goods, not another assignment for the party. If he tells the PCs this while selling goods earlier, the later arrival is a continuation of the same event. Preserve his previously promised discount.

Jord reaches Ledger House seeking a room whether the party witnesses it or not. If the group never returns, Brakkus can tell them about his arrival later; do not contrive Jord following them from shop to shop.

entries.name: Bishop Brann: The People Who Remain
entries: Brann remains in the city because his congregation, the poor, and the people who rely on his temple did not leave when the Council did. He can talk about how the Crown affects ordinary residents, funerals, records, access to healing and charity, rather than focusing only on Pepper.

Brann remembers the Council's original judgment. He does not declare a pardon, fabricate lost records or offer to conceal evidence. He need not volunteer Pepper's name to royal officials who have not asked him for it.
He and Jord need not agree with one another; Brann's concern for residents and Jord's practical concerns are distinct. Neither has to tell the party to oppose the Crown.

Brann comes looking for Brakkus, carrying the former Council's already-owed Kellan's Well contract payment. Total 300 gp; Jarrock 100 gp, Aaron 100 gp, Arunem 100 gp, Pepper 0 gp because her first compulsory Council mission was unpaid. If one is absent, Brann keeps that share until delivery. Do not confuse this payment with the prior 300 gp Brann paid the party for returning Blackstone's reliquary, or with the 375 gp recoverable at the Well.

If the party asks why Brann has the money after the Council left: the Council entrusted him with 300 gp for the other adventurers' Kellan's Well contract shares before its departure. He was the custodian of the money, not an offscreen witness to the fight; the party's return and report allow him to hand it over. There was never a requirement for the party to restore the sluice.

If the PCs have not reached Ledger House when Brann visits, Brakkus knows the payment is ready and Brann holds their undelivered shares for later collection. Do not assume funds were already received or add them to inventory until a player character actually accepts the money.

entries.name: Tulcornix Avemvir: Guaranteed Late-Session Arrival
entries: Tulcornix Avemvir is Kaleb's adopted brother, an aarakocra. His appearance during this session is non-negotiable. He brings the news that Kaleb's wife has been placed in indentured service under the Crown and needs to be rescued.

Plan Tulcornix's arrival only after the party has experienced the changed city and Brakkus's conversations. He deliberately tracks Pepper through plausible witness information. His confrontation and news of Elowen's indenture are the FINAL MOMENTS of Session 4; stop play immediately after the reveal. His longer conversation, the party's response, and any rescue proceed in Session 5.

He deliberately seeks Pepper because he knows she killed Kaleb and wants her to save Kaleb's wife Elowen. He confronts her at the close of Session 4. His feelings and request are his own; the party's choices begin in Session 5.

Treat the arrival and accusation as the cliffhanger, not a 15–30 minute conversation. Do not resolve or even begin the worksite rescue after this arrival in Session 4. The subsequent conversation can breathe at the beginning of Session 5.

Tulcornix has a conspicuously splinted and injured wing; he cannot safely fly when he arrives. While doing paid hauling/loading work at the street-facing Cardon Weavehouse annex to be near his sister-in-law, a shifting loom timber struck it. This was a worksite accident, not a secret attempt to silence him. He is able to walk, speak, and seek the party.

If a character applies appropriate healing magic, allow Tulcornix's injured wing to mend enough for flight. This doesn't solve his problem: Elowen remains subject to a Crown indenture in a watched worksite.

Tulcornix can name Cardon Weavehouse immediately, has personally seen Elowen in the annex, knows which entrance workers use, and can guide the party there. Core information is not gated by a skill check. He does not know the old compound's entire interior.
Opening option: "Kaleb's wife is at the Cardon Weavehouse. They call it a debt. They won't let her leave. I tried to get closer—" He indicates his splinted wing. "I need help getting her out."

Tulcornix deliberately seeks PEPPER, not Brakkus. He already knows that Pepper killed Kaleb, his adopted brother; he has not forgiven her. He knows the adventurers' connection to Ledger House, but if they relocate, he can ask people where Pepper went rather than miraculously appearing at her exact position.

Use this exact line as the closing confrontation with Pepper: 'You killed my brother, the stain of his blood will never leave your hands, save his wife and you might cleanse your soul.' The essential news that Elowen is held under Crown indenture at Cardon Weavehouse accompanies this final beat. If Pepper wants to challenge him, resolve the exchange when play resumes in Session 5. If she refuses, he can then look for other help; do not play that outcome during Session 4.

entries.name: Pepper: Existing Sentence, Low Administrative Priority
entries: {@b Confirmed sentence.} Pepper, a cleric, completed the first unpaid mission at Kellan's Well; the former Council ordered four further missions, to be paid normally, for her role in Kaleb's murder. This judgment is still unresolved. Do not turn it into a pardon, an acquittal, or a new service contract with the Crown.

{@b Practical effect of the changeover.} The Crown has an entire city's ownership records, government offices, revenue, trading rights and old contracts to review. Pepper's old Council-service file is not high on its list. Royal officers have not proactively taken up her case and there is no standing warrant or scheduled arrest scene created solely for this interlude.

{@b Brakkus's position.} Brakkus's supervision of Pepper's house arrest was performed for the former Council. That government has departed. With no new lawful directions that he has accepted, Brakkus will not continue to detain her on its behalf, will not volunteer her name to the Crown, and will not chase her into obedience. This is his own boundary, not a declaration that Pepper is legally pardoned.

{@b Practical suggestion.} Jord, as a merchant accustomed to bureaucratic delays, can suggest that Pepper stay under the Crown's radar. If she or someone else raises the topic with Bishop Brann, he can acknowledge that the old sentence has not been formally resolved, but he is not volunteering it to royal authorities.

{@b Player freedom.} Pepper and the other characters are free to take jobs, oppose the Crown, keep a low profile, or seek a formal legal resolution. Do not steer the party into working for the Crown to satisfy the old Council's five-mission sentence. If Pepper's status becomes relevant later, it must follow credible discovery or a choice at the table, not a hidden timer, an automatic patrol check, or a forced quest.

{@b Personal consequences remain.} Kaleb's murder, Jarrock reporting Pepper, her refusal to heal Jarrock, and Kaleb's surviving family remain part of the world. None are erased by paperwork becoming low priority. Pepper's resentment-driven looting has been of enemy property only; don't invent attacks on civilians or coerce an apology.
{@b Keep this brief.} Establish the practical advice if the topic arises; let the discussion move on. This is continuity maintenance, not the session's plot.

entries.name: Kaleb's Family and Tulcornix Avemvir
entries: Kaleb's wife is now an indentured servant of the Crown. His adopted brother Tulcornix Avemvir is an aarakocra who {@b must arrive during this session} and report that she needs help. Plan his appearance as the final major story beat, after the other people and the city have had space; his arrival is not optional.

Kaleb's widow is Elowen, an unwilling Crown-indenture textile worker in the street-facing Cardon Weavehouse annex. She is alive, can speak for herself, and is working in the cloth-sorting area. Her contract is not related to Pepper's old Council-service judgment. Elowen's daughter is currently safe with a trusted neighbor in Bellweather; her health and future need for healing remain unplayed, and no demand that Pepper heal her is imposed.

The public work ledger lists a made-up 'municipal recovery debt' of 150 gp and a royal processing fee of 50 gp, total 200 gp for an outright discharge, but this is the Crown's asserted price, not proof the indenture is just. Evidence, advocacy, a petition, negotiation, rescue or other actions can change the situation. There is no mandatory buyout.

While the Crown administers a street-facing work annex, Perrin's family claim, the old Weavehouse map, and previous unplayed occupants deeper in the property remain unresolved. Do not make Perrin the author of this indenture or use old Chapter 8 enemies as automatic reinforcements.
Tulcornix's arrival closes Session 4 with a request arising from his grief and Elowen's need. What Pepper and the party do with that request is Session 5 content.

Tulcornix's arrival is the Session 4 closing beat even if the group changes location; track Pepper through credible reports, without teleportation. If the party independently learns of Elowen BEFORE his arrival, he still seeks Pepper personally, and his confrontation is the final scene. Do not continue afterward.
A prior outline connected Kaleb's widow and daughter to a healing request. Do not require that exact request unless it still fits the circumstances and current story.

The Crown's Royal Municipal Recovery Assessment retroactively claims repayment for public services provided under the former free-city government, such as roads, sanitation, the watch and the waterworks. The Crown used municipal records obtained before the transfer to prepare charges. Elowen's household is assessed 150 gp and a 50 gp discharge-processing fee, total 200 gp. She was already working at the textile annex, which was commandeered, allowing officials to impose labor confinement quickly. Others have received notices; enforcement is patchy in the first hours, not every Bellweather household has been arrested. The assessment is legally asserted by the Crown, not demonstrated to be fair.

entries.name: If They Reach Cardon Weavehouse Before Tulcornix — or in Session 5
entries: The party can visit the textile work annex without running the entire older Weavehouse adventure. It has a public loading yard and work counter, staff-only door, cloth-sorting room, and ledger desk, with no need for an additional tactical map unless a fight develops.

Present at the street-facing annex: two uniformed watchmen ({@creature Guard|XMM}), one clerk ({@creature Commoner|XMM}), six ordinary laborers including Elowen. Those are all guards assigned to this annex for the present scene. Do not summon unlisted Chapter 8 occupants as a surprise wave.

The clerk will allow general questions and public-counter business. The work ledger openly identifies Elowen, her assignment, and the 150 gp + 50 gp claimed debt/processing charges. Workers cannot leave their contracts voluntarily. The watchmen prevent unauthorized departures, but do not attack mere visitors.

Let plausible plans work: submit or challenge the bond at Koven House, bargain or buy out the debt, speak with Elowen, forge an authorization, create a distraction, quietly extract her, or confront the guards. A reasonable public inquiry needs no roll. For disputed access use DC 13 Charisma (Deception or Persuasion) as appropriate; to open a secured staff latch use DC 15 Dexterity (Thieves' Tools), or DC 15 Strength (Athletics) to force. Obvious clever approaches succeed without checks. The watchmen can withdraw or surrender if overwhelmed, not fight suicidally.

Koven House's ground-floor public registry accepts paperwork and inquiries without a check; a clerk can identify the Cardon annex and bond office. It does not automatically search for Pepper's obsolete Council sentence. A higher official's involvement follows player actions, not a forced royal meeting.

Elowen wants her freedom and return to her daughter. She can speak for herself and is not automatically grateful to Pepper. This site's mechanics exist for Session 5, OR for the unusual case that the PCs discover and voluntarily visit the annex independently BEFORE Tulcornix has appeared in Session 4. Once Tulcornix appears, Session 4 ends; do not run an annex scene after the arrival.

The public counter has a work ledger citing Elowen's 150 gp Municipal Recovery Assessment and 50 gp discharge fee. The clerk explains that Crown staff prepared assessments from transferred Council records and names the Koven House registry for a petition or discharge papers. Public questions and sight of the ledger require no check. Existing two guards, one clerk and six workers remain the COMPLETE immediate annex roster; no surprise Chapter 8 reinforcements.

entries.name: Running a 3.5-Hour Social Session
entries: Flexible 3.5-hour target: Noren decision at the Well 10–25 minutes; city impressions 15–30; shopping and merchant questioning 30–75; Brakkus and Jord/Brann at Ledger House 40–75; Tulcornix's arrival, accusation and news about Elowen as a SHORT FINAL BEAT (3–8 minutes). Stop at his arrival and reveal. Session 5 begins with any reply, negotiation, investigation, or rescue.
Prepare NPC motives, current stakes, and consequences rather than a mandatory sequence. Give each player an opening to state a goal, and follow the actions the table actually chooses.

{@b Session priority.} Brakkus asks the party about their lives, Jord seeks lodging and Brann brings the Council money. Pepper's sentence is background. Tulcornix arrives specifically for Pepper as the final scene. No Elowen planning, negotiation or rescue takes place afterward in Session 4.

{@b Opposition is an option, not a contract.} The party is free to oppose, tolerate, exploit or ignore the Crown. Do not have Brakkus, Jord or Brann recruit the group as a mandatory resistance cell. Respect decisions even when they spoil planned pacing.
Keep several kinds of pressure available: moral disagreement, paperwork, labor disputes, divided loyalties, an ordinary favor, a celebration, a credible threat. None has to happen.
An antagonistic official can say no, call for guards, negotiate, or walk away as circumstances warrant. Do not roll initiative merely because the session needs an action scene.

Before Tulcornix arrives, record what the party learned, purchased, whom they helped or alienated, and what happened to both prisoners. Deliver Tulcornix's accusation and Elowen revelation, end the session, and begin the party's response next time.

Expect store customers to ask who governs, where the Council went, who received payment for the sale, whether old judgments still apply and whether guards have changed. Each shopkeeper's distinct knowledge and responses are in Appendix J. Don't require players to attend a separate briefing after shopping.

entries.name: Rewards and Advancement
entries: No automatic combat reward or encounter treasure is attached to this chapter. Specific assistance, favors, contacts, or money should reflect what characters actually accomplish.

This is the first post-Kellan's Well chapter; do not apply the superseded Koven criminal-network treasure package or award levels for scenes that did not happen. Level progression for the Crown-era story is deliberately open.
The following chapters contain established geographical/adventure assets but pre-Crown political scaffolding. Use Appendix I for what is current.

Outstanding Council contract money for clearing Kellan's Well: 300 gp delivered by Bishop Brann, 100 gp each to Jarrock, Aaron and Arunem, no compensation to Pepper for the first mandatory job. Track actual receipt; don't double-pay. Separate from previous Blackstone reliquary reward and fixed Well loot.

data.name: Chapter 7: Reconquest of Savin Keep

entries.name: Crown-Era Adaptation Notice — Unplayed Material
entries: This chapter retains usable locations, DM maps, NPCs, clues, encounter elements, and reward ideas from the pre-Crown reclamation outline. It has NOT yet been reconciled with the Council's completed sale of Bellweather to the Crown.

Any proposed Council contract, Council payment, Council authority, Perrin promotion to Council leadership, fixed plot sequence, or automatic level advancement written below is provisional, not current campaign canon. Choose a credible sponsor and political state when the party reaches this site; do not invent a restored Council or a predetermined royal overthrow.
Appendix I governs established facts. Preserve independent motives and genuine alternatives; do not treat the former outline as a script.
{@b Recommended level:} 5

entries.name: Chapter Overview
entries: {@b Chapter purpose.} Secure Savin Keep, free its bound defenders, and recover the first strong historical evidence of Tyren.
Bellweather needs Savin Keep to secure the harbor approach, but the ruined keep is still defended by undead bound to old orders.
Holding Savin Keep gives the city a strategic foothold and yields historical evidence naming Tyren as a force connected to Bellweather’s earlier fall.
{@b Leads onward.} The Council approves an expedition to Cardon Weavehouse, where property, occupants, and old records collide.

entries.name: Running the Chapter
entries: {@b Primary objectives.} Solve/bypass the undead defenses, break the binding, hold the keep during the counterattack.
{@b Player agency.} Research before departure, parley with bound spirits, use passwords, or force a military solution.
{@b Fail forward.} Passwords and historical clues have redundant sources. Missing one changes difficulty, not solvability.

{@b Rest and pressure.} Safe long rests are available back at Ledger House. Inside the active adventure site, resting gives opposing factions time to reposition unless the characters secure a defensible refuge.

### ##### Treasure Override Keep the {@item Potion of Heroism}, the hidden historical records, and either a {@item +1 Warhammer} or {@item +1 Shield}. Convert the remaining stockpile of permanent magic weapons into about {@b 700 gp} of legitimate salvage and ceremonial equipment; the Council separately pays 1,000 gp for reclaiming the keep.

entries.name: Encounter Guidance
entries: Keep the undead premise and use the exact finite rosters in the Table-Ready Session Package: 6 {@creature Skeleton|XMM|Skeletons} and 2 {@creature Zombie|XMM|Zombies} at the gate, 1 {@creature Wight|XMM} and 4 Skeletons at the Command Stone, and the listed Hobgoblin/Worg counterattack. The {@creature Ochre Jelly|XMM} remains an optional exploration encounter. Do not add Bugbears or additional waves unless a later campaign change explicitly adds them.

entries.name: Table-Ready Session Package
entries: {@b Milestone.} The party enters Savin Keep at level 5 and normally remains level 5 afterward; completing the Savin Keep + Cardon Weavehouse arc advances the party to level 6.

{@b Finite defenders.} Gate: 6 {@creature Skeleton|XMM|Skeletons} and 2 {@creature Zombie|XMM|Zombies}. Command Stone: 1 {@creature Wight|XMM} and 4 Skeletons. Counterattack: 1 {@creature Hobgoblin Captain|XMM}, 4 {@creature Hobgoblin Warrior|XMM|Hobgoblin Warriors}, and 2 {@creature Worg|XMM|Worgs}. The kitchen {@creature Ochre Jelly|XMM} is optional exploration pressure, not part of the military roster.

{@b Undead state.} The gate guardians remain passive toward characters who use the correct challenge-and-response. Destroying or bypassing them does not summon replacements. Breaking the Command Stone ends the old defensive binding and prevents remaining undead from coordinating.

{@b Counterattack trigger.} The Tyren-aligned force lands when the party reaches the watchtower interior or visibly breaks the keep's binding, whichever happens first. It enters from the dock and tries to seize the gate and burn records.

{@b Short rest.} Before the counterattack trigger, a secured room can support a Short Rest. After the trigger, a Short Rest gives the strike team time to occupy the dock and gate approaches; the rest can still complete if the party is secure, but the enemy gains that position.

{@b Hold clock.} If the party chooses to defend the keep, run 5 rounds. Bellweather reinforcements reach the island at the end of round 5. The attackers retreat if the captain falls or at least half the strike team is defeated.

{@b Records fail-forward.} The sealed Tyren report is in a fire-resistant document case and survives automatically. The attackers can destroy supporting correspondence, maps, or secondary context, but never the chapter's only Tyren clue.

{@b Useful DCs.} Interpret the password fragments DC 13 History or Investigation; spot the jelly's warning signs DC 13 Perception; force a jammed interior door DC 14 Athletics; stabilize a damaged record case DC 13 Arcana or appropriate tools.

{@b Pacing valve.} If time is short, passwords bypass the gate fight and the optional kitchen encounter disappears. If time remains, let the kitchen or a surviving undead patrol complicate exploration before the Command Stone.

entries.name: Counterattack Tactics
entries: The strike team arrives as one finite force: 1 {@creature Hobgoblin Captain|XMM}, 4 {@creature Hobgoblin Warrior|XMM|Hobgoblin Warriors}, and 2 {@creature Worg|XMM|Worgs}.

The Captain and 2 Warriors pressure the gate or dock. The other 2 Warriors carry oil and move toward the surviving records. The Worgs use speed to pin down characters who try to cover both objectives.

A Warrior adjacent to the secondary records can spend an action to spread oil and a later action to ignite it. One character adjacent to the fire can spend an action with water, blankets, magic, or another reasonable method to stop that ignition. The sealed Tyren report remains protected by the chapter's fail-forward rule.

If the party immediately overwhelms one group, the survivors converge on the remaining objective rather than standing in place to be killed. If the Captain falls or half the strike team is defeated, surviving attackers retreat toward the boats.

entries.name: Expected Session Shape
entries: Crossing and password discovery: about 20–30 minutes.
Gate/courtyard: 0 minutes if bypassed cleanly, otherwise about 30–45 minutes.
Barracks, shrine, and Command Stone: about 45–60 minutes.
Five-round counterattack: about 60–75 minutes.
Records and ownership aftermath: about 15–25 minutes.

{@b Keyed-area encounters.} When a scene and a keyed location describe the same encounter, use the roster and objective in the scene. Creatures listed only in the keyed reference apply when the characters explore that location outside the scene sequence.

entries.name: Location and Background Details
entries: Savin Keep stands on an island guarding Bellweather's harbor approach. The Council waits until nearby waters and landing points are reasonably secure before authorizing the mission. The objective is not to exterminate everything on the island; it is to make the keep safe enough for a permanent garrison and recover whatever records survived the fall.

entries.name: Approach and Passwords
entries: Three fragments—{@b Lux}, {@b Shestnik}, and {@b Samosud}—appear on old notes and plaques around the keep. Characters can learn that they were challenge-and-response phrases used by the final defenders. Discovering any two makes the third easier to infer from Ferren Marten's records. The passwords let the party bypass some undead guardians, but they are not required to complete the chapter.

entries.name: 1. Outside the Gate
entries: A weathered skeleton lies among reeds and stones. Its equipment is ruined, but a corroded medallion and partial note preserve two password fragments. A careful search also reveals tracks from a recent hostile reconnaissance team.

entries.name: 2. Gate and Courtyard
entries: The wooden gate is barely functional. Inside, the courtyard is patrolled by exactly 6 {@creature Skeleton|XMM|Skeletons} and 2 {@creature Zombie|XMM|Zombies} bound to the keep's final defense. The guardians ignore anyone who gives the correct password. Once combat begins, they fight until destroyed or the party withdraws beyond the gate.

entries.name: 3. Stable
entries: A collapsed stable contains an obvious patch of chemically damaged timber. Disturbing the rafters releases a {@creature Gray Ooze|XMM} or other corrosive creature or hazard appropriate to the party. The danger is telegraphed by dissolved nails and pitted stone.

entries.name: 4. Granary
entries: Pale fungus grows across old grain bins. A character proficient with Nature, Medicine, or an herbalism kit can identify a harmless restorative strain. Harvesting it yields one use that grants advantage on the next saving throw against the Frightened condition made before the next Long Rest.

entries.name: 5. Smithy
entries: The smithy is home to several territorial {@b Giant Frogs} or another small coastal predator. Behind the hearth lies a well-preserved weapon from the old garrison. Replace the original generic +1 weapon with one uncommon martial item appropriate to the party or with a named heirloom that can be returned to Bellweather for reputation.

entries.name: 6. Barracks
entries: The ruined barracks hold echoes of the final defenders. These manifestations do not attack. If greeted respectfully or with a password, they point out a hidden diary describing the unnatural coordination of the armies that destroyed Bellweather. This is an automatic clue to Tyren's historical influence.

entries.name: 7. Kitchen
entries: An {@creature Ochre Jelly|XMM} has spread through the ruined kitchen. A sour mineral odor, warped metal, and partially dissolved wood warn attentive characters. Roll Initiative normally if the party enters carelessly. The room contains salvage and one consumable reward after the creature is dealt with.

entries.name: 8. Entrance Hall — Counterattack
entries: When the party reaches the watchtower interior or visibly breaks the keep's binding, a Tyren-aligned strike team lands on the island to prevent reclamation. Use exactly 1 {@creature Hobgoblin Captain|XMM}, 4 {@creature Hobgoblin Warrior|XMM|Hobgoblin Warriors}, and 2 {@creature Worg|XMM|Worgs}. Their objective is to seize the gate and burn secondary records, not fight to the last creature. If the captain falls or half the force is defeated, the survivors withdraw toward their boats.
The undead guardians oppose the strike team as readily as they oppose the characters. Clever parties can exploit that conflict.

entries.name: 9. Armory
entries: Most racks are empty. An illusory wall conceals a surviving cache. Award one uncommon permanent item, one consumable, and mundane salvage rather than several stacking +1 items.

entries.name: 10. Officer's Quarters
entries: A nearly transparent predator—use an appropriate ooze, mimic-like creature, or {@creature Invisible Stalker|XMM} only if the party's tier supports it—has made this room its hunting ground. Scratches and dragged dust provide warning. A parchment here contains the final password fragment.

entries.name: 11. Old Chapel
entries: The spirit of {@b Ferren Marten}, last chaplain of Savin Keep, appears near the altar. He is not inherently hostile. If the party identifies themselves as Bellweather's reclaimers and treats the dead with respect, Ferren explains that Bellweather fell because powerful leaders were unnaturally unified by a force associated with a radiant pool. He names {@b Tyren}, {@b Edra}, and {@b Toran}, and points the party toward records once kept at Marren Library.

Ferren then releases the remaining defender-spirits from their duty. If attacked, use a {@creature Specter|XMM} or {@creature Wraith|XMM} chassis appropriate to the party, but the scene is intended as revelation rather than combat.

entries.name: Securing Savin Keep
entries: The mission succeeds when the party has broken the binding on the defenders, prevented the counterattack from destroying the site, and made the approach safe enough for a Council garrison. On return, shipping begins expanding almost immediately.

entries.name: Scene 1: The Crossing
entries: The party leads the first landing while a small Bellweather guard detachment waits offshore for a signal.

entries.name: What Happens
entries: Stealth or bad weather can conceal the boat. Bright light or loud magic alerts the gate.
Old signal bells begin ringing without visible hands as the party approaches.

entries.name: Clues and Discoveries
entries: The keep appears abandoned but reacts to intruders according to ancient routines.

entries.name: Consequences
entries: An undetected landing lets the party inspect the gate before combat.

entries.name: Scene 2: Gate and Courtyard
entries: Undead defenders continue commands issued during Bellweather’s last fall.

entries.name: What Happens
entries: They hold assigned posts and do not pursue far beyond them.

entries.name: Encounter
entries: 6 {@creature Skeleton|XMM|Skeletons}, 2 {@creature Zombie|XMM|Zombies}.

entries.name: Clues and Discoveries
entries: A guardroom tablet says “hold until relieved by lawful command,” implying the binding can be ended.

entries.name: Consequences
entries: Destroying every undead works, but learning the release phrase reduces later resistance.

entries.name: Scene 3: Barracks and Shrine
entries: A ruined shrine preserves the oath formula used by the last commander.

entries.name: What Happens
entries: Characters who search the shrine find the release phrase and learn that speaking it at the command stone can end the old watch.

entries.name: Clues and Discoveries
entries: The oath names the last commander and confirms the undead were defenders, not invaders.

entries.name: Consequences
entries: This discovery reframes the keep as a tragedy rather than a monster nest.

entries.name: Scene 4: Command Stone
entries: The binding focus is defended by the last commander’s wight.

entries.name: What Happens
entries: Speaking the release phrase causes ordinary skeletons to stop fighting immediately.

entries.name: Encounter
entries: 1 {@creature Wight|XMM}, 4 {@creature Skeleton|XMM|Skeletons}.

entries.name: Clues and Discoveries
entries: A sealed report names Tyren as a possessing force linked to disturbances around the Radiant Well generations ago.

entries.name: Consequences
entries: This is the first historical evidence that the present “Boss” may be connected to an older threat.

entries.name: Scene 5: Counterattack
entries: Living Tyren-aligned troops attack before Bellweather can occupy the keep.

entries.name: What Happens
entries: The party must hold either the dock or gate for 5 rounds. At the end of round 5, Bellweather reinforcements arrive.

entries.name: Encounter
entries: 1 {@creature Hobgoblin Captain|XMM}, 4 {@creature Hobgoblin Warrior|XMM|Hobgoblin Warriors}, 2 {@creature Worg|XMM|Worgs}.

entries.name: Consequences
entries: Holding the keep secures the harbor route and turns the site into a Bellweather garrison.

entries.name: Scene 6: Records of Ownership
entries: Old inventories recovered from the keep identify surviving archives tied to the Cardon family’s Weavehouse.

entries.name: What Happens
entries: Perrin requests access to the records and proposes reclaiming the Weavehouse next.

entries.name: Clues and Discoveries
entries: The records are genuine and establish a plausible Cardon claim.

entries.name: Consequences
entries: Do not level here. The party remains level 5; resolving the Savin Keep + Cardon Weavehouse arc advances the party to level 6.

entries.name: Transition to Chapter 8
entries: The Council approves an expedition to Cardon Weavehouse, where property, occupants, and old records collide.

entries.name: Rewards
entries: {@b Treasure and rewards.} Reclaiming Savin Keep earns a {@b 1,000 gp} civic/military payment plus about {@b 700 gp} in legitimate salvage and ceremonial equipment. Also award a Potion of Heroism and either a +1 Shield (default) or +1 Warhammer if the party needs a weapon. Historical records are evidence and civic leverage rather than saleable loot.

entries.name: Rewards
entries: These rewards are party totals for the campaign's four-character party.

items: {@b Spendable wealth.} 600–900 gp in military salvage and Council bounty.
{@b Consumables.} 2 useful consumables.
{@b Permanent magic.} 1 uncommon permanent item. A thoroughly searched concealed armory can hold a second uncommon item only if the party is behind the campaign reward curve.
{@b Story reward.} A Council garrison, expanded shipping security, and access to a strategic base.

Any proposed Council contract, Council payment, Council authority, Perrin promotion to Council leadership, fixed plot sequence, or automatic level advancement written below is provisional, not current campaign canon. Choose a credible sponsor and political state when the party reaches this site; do not invent a restored Council or a predetermined royal overthrow.
Appendix I governs established facts. Preserve independent motives and genuine alternatives; do not treat the former outline as a script.

Chapter 6 now prepares a Crown-indentured textile work annex facing the public street at Cardon Weavehouse, holding Elowen. This does not overwrite the old property map, settle Perrin's family claim, or confirm the unplayed Korrin occupation. Annex guard/clerk roster lives in Chapter 6. If players explore beyond the annex, reconcile the older occupation before using Chapter 8 rather than combining contradictory statuses or spawning old enemies as reinforcements.
