entries.name: Chapter Overview
entries: {@b Chapter purpose.} Reclaim the Cardon Weavehouse and force the party to confront the difference between public risk and private inheritance.
Perrin Cardon asks the Council to reclaim his family’s old Weavehouse, presenting the mission as both civic recovery and restoration of lawful ownership.
Whatever the decision, Perrin recovers enough wealth and documentation to become a much more influential figure in Bellweather.
{@b Leads onward.} The Weavehouse correspondence points toward Marren Library, where pre-fall scholars investigated the Radiant Well.

entries.name: Running the Chapter
entries: {@b Primary objectives.} Secure the building, identify the real ownership/treasure question, survive rival claims.
{@b Player agency.} Honor Cardon’s claim, challenge it, negotiate public use, or bargain for concessions.
{@b Fail forward.} The Cardon history is discoverable through multiple records and witnesses.

{@b Rest and pressure.} Safe long rests are available back at Ledger House. Inside the active adventure site, resting gives opposing factions time to reposition unless the characters secure a defensible refuge.

### ##### Treasure Override Most recovered wealth belongs to the property itself or the Cardon claim. Let the party recover {@b 500–750 gp} in immediate valuables and one uncommon permanent item at most. The larger economic reward is Cardon's restored fortune and rising influence.

entries.name: Encounter Guidance
entries: Use the finite population in the Table-Ready Session Package. The armed occupation is a social structure with dependents and coerced workers, not a respawning dungeon. The only optional creature hazard is one {@creature Ochre Jelly|XMM} in the collapsed wing.

entries.name: Table-Ready Session Package
entries: {@b Milestone.} The party enters the Weavehouse at level 5. Resolving the Savin Keep + Cardon Weavehouse arc advances the party to level 6.

{@b Population.} Armed: {@creature Korrin Vale|NCFA}, 4 {@creature Thug|XMM|Thugs}, 2 {@creature Scout|XMM|Scouts}, and 1 {@creature Cult Fanatic|XMM} guarding Tyren's correspondence. Noncombatants: about 10 dependents plus 2 coerced workers. They hide, flee, or surrender if given a safe route.

{@b Alarm drum.} If the drum sounds, Korrin and the 4 Thugs consolidate at the Main Hall while the 2 Scouts take cover overlooking the courtyard. The Cult Fanatic begins destroying correspondence at the end of round 2. No reinforcements arrive from outside the property.

{@b Evidence fail-forward.} If the shrine letters burn, the Records Vault contains a duplicate tribute schedule and witness statements establishing the same essential fact: Tyren rewards obedience, threatens independence, and coordinates multiple groups.

{@b Collapsed-wing hazard.} Crossing the unstable section requires DC 14 Acrobatics or a careful alternative. On a failed rushed crossing, the character falls through weak flooring, takes 2d6 bludgeoning damage, and lands Prone. One {@creature Ochre Jelly|XMM} can be used here only if an extra combat beat is useful.

{@b Short rest.} The garden/cistern can support a Short Rest after it is secured. During the hour, an alerted occupation consolidates as described above and the shrine leader starts destroying papers; no extra enemies appear.

{@b Social DCs.} Korrin hears a concrete safe-passage offer without a check if the party clearly controls the situation; otherwise DC 14 Persuasion gets him to negotiate. DC 13 Insight reveals Mara's main concern is time and safe relocation rather than ownership. The final property settlement is decided by evidence and advocacy, not one Persuasion roll.

{@b Morale.} Korrin surrenders if isolated and below half hit points. Thugs stand down if Korrin surrenders. Scouts flee if both routes to Korrin and the shrine are cut off. The Cult Fanatic flees once the papers are lost or secured.

{@b Pacing valve.} If time is short, successful talks with Mara reveal the Records Vault and let the party bypass one armed position. If time remains, use the collapsed-wing hazard or the shrine confrontation as an additional beat.

entries.name: Starting Positions
entries: Outer gates/courtyard: 2 {@creature Thug|XMM|Thugs}.
Watchpost: 2 {@creature Scout|XMM|Scouts}.
Main Hall: {@creature Korrin Vale|NCFA} and 2 Thugs.
Shrine: 1 {@creature Cult Fanatic|XMM}.

These are the entire armed population listed for the chapter. If the alarm drum sounds, they move from these positions into the consolidation pattern already described; do not add unnamed patrols or off-duty fighters.

entries.name: Expected Session Shape
entries: Perrin's claim and approach: about 20–30 minutes.
Contact with Mara and the residents: about 30–45 minutes.
Infiltration, negotiation, or armed confrontation: about 45–75 minutes.
Records Vault and shrine evidence: about 30–45 minutes.
Settlement and Perrin consequence: about 30 minutes.

{@b Keyed-area encounters.} When a scene and a keyed location describe the same encounter, use the roster and objective in the scene. Creatures listed only in the keyed reference apply when the characters explore that location outside the scene sequence.

entries.name: Perrin's Rise: Restored Wealth
entries: The Weavehouse is the turning point in Perrin's material power. He recovers enough wealth, documentation, and credit to hire protection, sponsor repairs, make loans, and reward political allies. Even if the party limits his property claim, he emerges from the chapter richer and more visible than before.
Do not present this as a secret coup. Residents should notice Cardon-funded work crews, guards, charitable gestures, and merchants suddenly taking his calls.

entries.name: Location and Background Details
entries: The Council authorizes reclamation of the old Cardon property after the surrounding route is reasonably secure. Perrin publicly frames the mission as civic recovery, but privately wants proof of ownership and the family cache returned to him.

Before departure, Perrin offers {@b Taren Vale}, an aging household retainer represented by a {@creature Scout|XMM} or {@creature Veteran|XMM} as appropriate. Taren remembers the old layout imperfectly and can sketch the broad plan. His private instruction is to identify Cardon heirlooms and report what the party finds. He does not steal from the characters or force the outcome.

If the party recovers disputed property, Perrin first attempts a legal claim through the Council. The characters can accept compensation, challenge the claim with records, negotiate public use, or demand an independent hearing. The Council is institutionally inclined to protect documented ownership, but it is not predetermined to side with Perrin. Reputation, evidence, and witnesses matter.

entries.name: Korrin's Occupation
entries: A Tyren-aligned mixed armed group under {@creature Korrin Vale|NCFA} controls the Weavehouse and charges the civilian residents for food and protection. The armed group is exactly Korrin, 4 {@creature Thug|XMM|Thugs}, 2 {@creature Scout|XMM|Scouts}, and 1 {@creature Cult Fanatic|XMM}. Species is not the faction's moral identity.
The complex also contains about 10 dependents and 2 coerced workers. They flee, hide, or surrender if given a safe route and never expand the combat roster.
The group uses an alarm drum. Once raised, the existing armed members consolidate around the courtyard, Main Hall, and shrine rather than spawning reinforcements.

entries.name: 1. Outer Gates and Courtyard
entries: The old Cardon crest is still visible beneath the occupation's angular red mark. Two {@creature Thug|XMM|Thugs} watch the courtyard. The party can infiltrate over a wall, bluff at a gate, enter through collapsed structures, or trigger a direct fight. If the alarm is raised, these Thugs fall back toward the Main Hall rather than waiting to die in the open.

entries.name: 2. Collapsed Wing
entries: Burned-out structures contain refuse, unstable flooring, and a corrosive ooze. The area also provides a concealed route around the main courtyard for characters willing to crawl through debris.

entries.name: 3. Watchpost
entries: Two {@creature Scout|XMM|Scouts} watch one approach from cover. Their duty roster contains Tyren's seal and references tribute demanded from multiple independent factions—useful evidence that the Boss is coordinating more than one group. If warned, they relocate to overlook the courtyard as described in the alarm state.

entries.name: 4–5. Former Servants' Quarters
entries: These rooms house junior guards and people low in the warband hierarchy. They are the easiest occupants to convince to stand down, especially if the party promises safe passage. One knows where prisoners and noncombatants are being kept.

entries.name: 6. Main Hall
entries: {@creature Korrin Vale|NCFA} uses this former reception hall as a command post with 2 {@creature Thug|XMM|Thugs}. Korrin's goal is to preserve control of the site and protect the people who depend on his group; once defeat is clear, he prefers terms to a pointless last stand.

entries.name: 7–9. Living Quarters
entries: These rooms contain dependents, wounded members, and off-duty retainers. Treat them as a social and moral complication, not an encounter quota. If the party indiscriminately attacks noncombatants, Neighborhoods & Workers and Independent Factions reputation suffer.

entries.name: 10. Garden
entries: The old kitchen garden has gone wild. A hidden cistern provides a quiet route between buildings and can serve as a defensible short-rest location once secured.

entries.name: 11. Cardon Bedroom and Cache
entries: The family cache is concealed behind old plaster. A ten-minute search finds it automatically; a successful DC 14 Intelligence (Investigation) check finds it immediately. The art objects are historically and legally significant, not merely loot. Their total market value is substantial, but the chapter's {@b Treasure Override} determines what portable wealth the party actually receives.
Finding the cache creates the chapter's central choice: return it to Perrin, place it in Council custody, use Marren Library records to challenge ownership, or negotiate a public settlement.

entries.name: 12. Shrine and Correspondence
entries: One {@creature Cult Fanatic|XMM} keeps Tyren's letters and tribute demands. The correspondence makes clear that Korrin's group is being rewarded for obedience and threatened for independence. If the alarm sounds, the fanatic begins destroying the letters at the end of round 2 as described in the Table-Ready Session Package.

entries.name: Resolution
entries: The site is reclaimed when the command structure is broken, civilians and dependents are no longer trapped inside, and the Council can occupy the property without immediate counterattack. What happens to the property itself is a political question, not a dungeon reward.

entries.name: Scene 1: Perrin’s Claim
entries: Perrin presents deeds showing that his family owned the Weavehouse before Bellweather fell.

entries.name: What Happens
entries: He asks the party to secure the property and preserve surviving records. He does not ask them to harm current occupants.

entries.name: NPC Behavior
entries: Perrin genuinely believes restored ownership will attract investment and stabilize Bellweather.

entries.name: Clues and Discoveries
entries: Workers warn that several families and a small armed band now use the complex.

entries.name: Consequences
entries: The party can seek relocation guarantees before entering.

entries.name: Scene 2: The Courtyard Occupants
entries: Civilian squatters live under the protection of a warband that charges them for food and safety.

entries.name: What Happens
entries: Speaking with civilians first identifies which structures contain fighters and which contain families.

entries.name: NPC Behavior
entries: Mara Pell, a halfling woman, speaks for the families and wants time plus guaranteed relocation. Korrin Vale leads the armed group and wants the stored goods.

{@b NPC description — Korrin Vale.} A broad, powerfully built dragonborn man in repaired military gear with no matching insignia left on it, Korrin has dark bronze scales, a chipped horn, and the bearing of a discharged soldier rather than a street tough. He keeps his weapons maintained, gives short orders, and becomes noticeably less certain when separated from his followers.

entries.name: Clues and Discoveries
entries: Residents know the records vault has remained sealed.

entries.name: Consequences
entries: Treating civilians fairly earns durable neighborhood support.

entries.name: Scene 3: Armed Wing
entries: Korrin’s fighters hold the warehouse and counting room.

entries.name: What Happens
entries: Korrin surrenders if isolated and reduced below half hit points. Civilians do not fight unless attacked.

entries.name: NPC Behavior
entries: {@creature Korrin Vale|NCFA} uses the Warrior Veteran stat block.

entries.name: Encounter
entries: 1 {@creature Veteran|XMM}, 4 {@creature Thug|XMM|Thugs}, 2 {@creature Scout|XMM|Scouts}.

entries.name: Consequences
entries: A negotiated surrender prevents unnecessary civilian displacement.

entries.name: Scene 4: Records Vault
entries: The sealed vault contains deeds, payrolls, debt books, and customer inventories.

entries.name: What Happens
entries: Separate the documents into Cardon property, worker property, customer consignments, and public historical records.

entries.name: Clues and Discoveries
entries: The building belongs to the Cardon family, but not everything inside does. Correspondence mentions scholars at Marren Library studying “radiant disturbances” before the fall.

entries.name: Consequences
entries: The party’s handling of the records establishes a precedent others later cite.

entries.name: Scene 5: The Settlement
entries: Perrin, residents, workers’ descendants, and Council clerks make competing claims after the danger is gone.

entries.name: What Happens
entries: The party can advocate for strict deed ownership, compensation and relocation, shared recovery, or another arrangement.

entries.name: NPC Behavior
entries: Perrin accepts a lawful compromise in public even if it limits his gain; he remembers who opposed him.

entries.name: Consequences
entries: Perrin gains enough wealth and standing to become a major Council voice. Marren Library becomes the obvious next historical target.

entries.name: Optional Jarrock Thread: Rena Dask
entries: Rena Dask attends or sends a statement on behalf of reclamation crews. She does not claim the Cardon family has no rights; she argues that workers who took the physical risks of reopening the property should receive enforceable safety standards, compensation, or a defined public benefit rather than only wages and thanks.

If Jarrock supports her automatically, have Rena acknowledge a legitimate Cardon claim the evidence actually supports. If he dismisses her automatically, have her point to a concrete injury, unpaid cost, or public subsidy. Keep the question difficult rather than making either side a caricature.

entries.name: Transition to Chapter 9
entries: The Weavehouse correspondence points toward Marren Library, where pre-fall scholars investigated the Radiant Well.

entries.name: Rewards
entries: {@b Treasure and rewards.} Resolve the chapter at about {@b 2,000 gp} of total party economic value: roughly {@b 1,200 gp} in payment, restitution, or lawful recovery awards and {@b 800 gp} in immediately portable coin, jewelry, or uncontested valuables. Major property assets remain in legal process. Also award {@b 2 consumables} and one uncommon permanent item, default {@b Sending Stones}.

entries.name: Rewards
entries: These rewards are party totals for the campaign's four-character party.

items: {@b Spendable wealth.} About 2,000 gp of total party economic value: roughly 1,200 gp in payment/restitution and 800 gp in uncontested portable valuables.
{@b Consumables.} 2 useful consumables.
{@b Permanent magic.} 1 uncommon permanent item, default Sending Stones, unless another item better fills an existing party gap.
{@b Story reward.} Legal leverage over Perrin Cardon, testimony from residents and workers, and a precedent for how Bellweather handles reclaimed private property.

data.name: Chapter 9: Marren Library

entries.name: Crown-Era Adaptation Notice — Unplayed Material
entries: This chapter retains usable locations, DM maps, NPCs, clues, encounter elements, and reward ideas from the pre-Crown reclamation outline. It has NOT yet been reconciled with the Council's completed sale of Bellweather to the Crown.

Any proposed Council contract, Council payment, Council authority, Perrin promotion to Council leadership, fixed plot sequence, or automatic level advancement written below is provisional, not current campaign canon. Choose a credible sponsor and political state when the party reaches this site; do not invent a restored Council or a predetermined royal overthrow.
Appendix I governs established facts. Preserve independent motives and genuine alternatives; do not treat the former outline as a script.
{@b Recommended level:} 6

entries.name: Chapter Overview
entries: {@b Chapter purpose.} Recover Bellweather’s documentary memory and reveal Tyren as a possessing intelligence linked to the Radiant Well.
Bellweather gains access to Marren Library, one of the best surviving collections of pre-fall records.
By the end of the chapter, the party should understand that Tyren is not merely a warlord but a possessing intelligence linked to the Radiant Well.
{@b Leads onward.} With valuable districts reopening, old families and investors begin pressing claims in the Mansion District.

entries.name: Running the Chapter
entries: {@b Primary objectives.} Preserve records, identify Radiant Well references, choose who receives copies.
{@b Player agency.} Work for Cardon, work for the Council, copy records independently, or involve scholars/temples.
{@b Fail forward.} Core Radiant Well clues are guaranteed; checks determine how complete and private the discovery is.

{@b Rest and pressure.} Safe long rests are available back at Ledger House. Inside the active adventure site, resting gives opposing factions time to reposition unless the characters secure a defensible refuge.

### ##### Treasure Override Knowledge is the reward. Give the party 2–4 useful spell scrolls appropriate to their level, one uncommon or rare utility item, and valuable manuscripts worth {@b 500 gp} if sold—or much more as leverage with scholars and the Council.

entries.name: Encounter Guidance
entries: Use the exact finite opposition in the Table-Ready Session Package. The chapter's difficulty comes from simultaneous preservation objectives and social choices, not from turning the library into a monster gauntlet. Gargoyles, Tessa's four-person crew, the Specter, and the optional Mimic are the full encounter menu.

entries.name: Table-Ready Session Package
entries: {@b Milestone.} The party enters the Marren/Mansions arc at level 6. Resolving Marren Library and the associated Bellweather property-case arc advances the party to level 7.

{@b Finite opposition.} 2 {@creature Gargoyle|XMM|Gargoyles} at the monument, Tessa Marr plus 3 other {@creature Scout|XMM|Scouts}, and 1 {@creature Specter|XMM} guarding the restricted collection. One {@creature Mimic|XMM} in the supply room is an optional pacing encounter, not a required fight.

{@b Fire clock.} Once the stacks fire becomes active, run 4 rounds. The party needs 5 total successful fire-control actions before the end of round 4. An appropriate area spell or especially strong fictional solution can count as 2 successes; otherwise use DC 13 with a relevant ability or tool. Failed attempts cost the action and can trigger the fire-failure consequences, but do not erase earlier successes.

{@b Fire failure.} Track total failed fire-control attempts. At 2 failures, one secondary collection is lost. If the party reaches the end of round 4 without 5 successes, a second secondary collection and up to 500 gp of manuscript value are lost. The Restricted Stacks and essential Tyren/Radiant Well revelations survive.

{@b Scavenger behavior.} Tessa's crew wants specified research, not a massacre. They stop fighting if Tessa is reduced below half hit points, if 2 Scouts fall, or if the party offers a safe exit without the commissioned papers. They help with the fire if convinced their own escape depends on it.

{@b Guardian behavior.} The Gargoyles defend only the monument area. The Specter begins with conversation and attacks only if the Restricted Stacks are threatened, deliberately damaged, or forced open after its warning.

{@b Short rest.} A secured group-study room can support a Short Rest after the scavenger situation is settled. If the fire has already started, it continues during the hour and automatically reaches its failure state unless the party solves it first.

{@b Useful DCs.} Fire control DC 13; suppress the office ward DC 15 Arcana; resist the ward DC 14 Wisdom; identify which archive copy is original DC 14 Investigation; gain the Specter's trust with respectful handling and a concrete preservation plan DC 14 Persuasion or Religion.
{@b Pacing valve.} If time is short, the Gargoyles remain dormant and the optional Mimic is absent. If time remains, activate one of those encounters after the essential archive work is complete.

entries.name: Fire and Scavenger Playtest
entries: If the party negotiates successfully with Tessa, her crew helps evacuate books but does not automatically solve the blaze; the party still runs the 5-success fire clock.

If negotiation fails, Tessa and 3 {@creature Scout|XMM|Scouts} use tables and shelving as cover and try to leave with their commissioned books. They do not stand in a firing line. The party now has to decide how many actions to spend on the fire versus stopping the crew.

Tessa's crew stops fighting if Tessa drops below half hit points, 2 Scouts go down, or the party offers safe exit without the commissioned research. Once a truce is reached, surviving scavengers can spend their turns moving books to safety, but their actions do not count toward the party's 5 fire-control successes.
The goal is pressure, not lethality. Against this party, four Scouts alone are not a meaningful combat threat; the fire is what makes their presence matter.

entries.name: Expected Session Shape
entries: Arrival and initial survey: about 20–30 minutes.
Reading room and the fire/scavenger crisis: about 60–75 minutes.
Master Librarian chamber and Restricted Stacks: about 45–60 minutes.
Property archives and publication choice: about 30 minutes.
The Bellweather property case can take the final 20–40 minutes or open the next session.

{@b Keyed-area encounters.} When a scene and a keyed location describe the same encounter, use the roster and objective in the scene. Creatures listed only in the keyed reference apply when the characters explore that location outside the scene sequence.

entries.name: Perrin's Rise: Administrative Network
entries: Perrin uses wealth and archive access to cultivate clerks, recordkeepers, merchants, and junior officials. If the party gives him records, the network grows faster; if they resist, he builds it through copies, public filings, favors, and patronage.
He still does not control the Council, but he increasingly understands which forms, seals, schedules, and staff actually make Bellweather's government function.

entries.name: Marren Library Tactical Map Key
entries: The replacement Marren Library map is intentionally compact and table-buildable. Use the numbered areas below as the authoritative geography for Chapter 9. The Cardon Weavehouse map remains unchanged.

entries.name: Location and Background Details
entries: Marren Library is valuable because it contains the documentary memory Bellweather lost when the city fell. Perrin wants specific records concerning old property, the Radiant Well, and the Cardon family's claims. The Council publicly describes the mission as preservation.

entries.name: Entering the Library
entries: The building is damaged but recognizable. Collapsed walls create multiple entrances. The party's challenge is less about clearing every room than about finding the right collections while protecting fragile records from hazards and opportunists.

entries.name: 1. Entrance & Foyer
entries: The library’s main entrance is damaged but usable. A small reception desk, display cases, and scattered civic notices make the building’s former public function obvious. Characters who pause here can identify the safest routes into the reading room and offices without a check.

entries.name: 2. Reading Room
entries: This broad central room is the party’s primary research space. Long tables and open shelves create clear lanes of movement and plentiful half-cover. Searching here reveals catalog references pointing toward the Librarian’s Office, Reference Alcove, General Stacks, and Restricted Stacks.

entries.name: 3. Librarian’s Office
entries: The head librarian’s office contains administrative ledgers, accession lists, property correspondence, and notes connecting several pre-fall researchers to the Radiant Well. A meaningful search automatically identifies which collections contain the campaign’s essential historical clues.

entries.name: 4. Study Room
entries: A quiet group-study chamber with a large table and wall shelving. Independent scholars, scavengers, or another intelligent faction can be encountered here. Treat this as a social-first scene: cooperation can produce catalog information, while threats or violence risk damage to nearby records.

entries.name: 5. Reference Alcove
entries: Rare and frequently consulted works are kept here. One {@creature Animated Armor|XMM} and two {@creature Flying Sword|XMM} guardians protect the sealed reference cases. They activate only when someone forces a case or removes protected material without satisfying the library’s old authorization mechanism.

entries.name: 6. General Stacks
entries: The largest surviving collection fills tightly spaced rows. A {@creature Basilisk|XMM} has nested among damaged shelves; toppled cases and narrow aisles create cover and movement choices. The party can bypass it by using the Reading Room and Reference Alcove routes rather than treating the stacks as a mandatory fight.

entries.name: 7. Scribe Room
entries: Copying desks, inks, blank folios, and preservation supplies remain usable. Once the party finds important records, this room lets them make controlled copies before deciding who receives originals. Ten minutes of careful work produces a serviceable duplicate of one discovered document set.

entries.name: 8. Restricted Stacks
entries: The locked restricted collection contains the strongest Radiant Well and possession material. A {@creature Specter|XMM} tied to the old library serves as a social-first guardian and attacks only if the collection is threatened or deliberately destroyed. The essential revelations here are automatic: Tyren can survive by transferring between hosts, and the Radiant Well can admit or alter consciousness. The pre-fall “no cause for alarm” Council circular is also stored here.

entries.name: 9. Storage
entries: Supply crates, book carts, damaged archival boxes, and wrapped salvage fill this small room. One suspicious container can be a {@creature Mimic|XMM} if an extra encounter is useful; otherwise this area holds preservation materials and the chapter’s utility-item reward rather than another compulsory fight.

entries.name: 4–6. Reading Rooms and Entrance Hall
entries: These areas contain rotted furniture, faded murals, and scattered fragments. They are useful for quiet exploration and for foreshadowing the institution Bellweather once was rather than for mandatory combat.

entries.name: 8–11. Workrooms and Carrels
entries: Most supplies are ruined, but careful salvage can recover a modest amount of gold leaf, inks, vellum, and tools. Use these as crafting materials or civic salvage rather than a large cash payout.

entries.name: The Historical Refrain
entries: Among pre-fall Council records is the circular quoted earlier in this chapter: {@b “There is no cause for alarm.”} It was issued while reports of coordinated hostile movement were already accumulating. This is the adventure's clearest historical echo of the title.

entries.name: Resolution
entries: The party succeeds by securing the most important records and determining how they will be held. Giving everything to Perrin strengthens him. Putting the archive under Council or independent stewardship creates different political consequences. The essential Tyren clues are preserved regardless.

entries.name: Scene 1: Reaching the Library
entries: The library is structurally damaged and occupied by scavengers and magical hazards. The party’s objective is preservation as much as exploration.

entries.name: What Happens
entries: A smoke plume from one wing means some records are already in danger. Characters can enter through the garden court, main hall, or a broken upper window.

If the party spends a full hour elsewhere after reaching the library without investigating the smoke and heat, one minor collection is lost before Scene 3 begins. Once the active blaze is confronted, use the four-round Fire Clock instead of tracking additional hours.

entries.name: Clues and Discoveries
entries: Bellweather scholars provide a list of three priority collections: civic annals, magical research, and property records.

entries.name: Consequences
entries: The party must choose what to protect first, giving the expedition an immediate priority.

entries.name: Scene 2: Reading Room and Stacks
entries: The reading room opens into damaged stacks where old guardians and ruin predators can complicate the search.

entries.name: What Happens
entries: Moving carefully reveals signs of recent human passage leading to the stacks.

entries.name: Encounter
entries: Use 2 {@creature Gargoyle|XMM|Gargoyles} if the party disturbs the central monument. They defend the courtyard only.

entries.name: Clues and Discoveries
entries: A satchel dropped by scavengers contains copied page numbers from the magical research wing. Someone else is looking for the same records.

entries.name: Consequences
entries: Capturing or tracking the scavengers can reveal that they were paid anonymously.

entries.name: Scene 3: Stacks and Fire
entries: A collapsed lamp has started a spreading fire while frightened scavengers try to remove selected volumes.

entries.name: What Happens
entries: Five successful fire-control actions using water, magic, blankets, tools, or DC 13 ability checks contain the fire before the end of round 4. Especially effective area magic or a strong fictional solution can count as 2 successes.
The scavengers surrender if cornered; they were hired to recover specific research, not burn the building.

entries.name: NPC Behavior
entries: Their leader, Tessa Marr, was promised 200 gp by a masked intermediary and knows only a drop location.

{@b NPC description — Tessa Marr.} A rangy wood elf woman who looks young by elven standards, tall and narrow-built, with cropped auburn hair, a patched hooded coat, and the restless gaze of someone always measuring distance to the nearest exit. She carries herself like a scout rather than a bruiser and speaks quickly once she realizes a fight is going against her.

entries.name: Encounter
entries: Use 4 {@creature Scout|XMM|Scouts} if negotiation fails.

entries.name: Clues and Discoveries
entries: The requested volumes concern the Radiant Well, possession, and “personality transference.”

entries.name: Consequences
entries: Saving the stacks earns scholar and public goodwill.

entries.name: Scene 4: Master Librarian’s Chamber
entries: The locked chamber contains the most coherent pre-fall account of Tyren.

entries.name: What Happens
entries: A damaged ward triggers when the desk is forced. DC 15 Intelligence (Arcana) or dispel magic suppresses it; otherwise each creature in the room makes a DC 14 Wisdom save or is frightened until the end of its next turn.

entries.name: Clues and Discoveries
entries: The journal states that Tyren is an intelligence capable of occupying living hosts. The Radiant Well amplifies or facilitates the transfer. The author believed destroying a host would not necessarily destroy Tyren.

entries.name: Consequences
entries: This changes the campaign’s central question from “Who is the Boss?” to “What intelligence is possessing the figure the factions call the Boss, and how does it move between hosts?”

entries.name: Scene 5: Property Archives
entries: The property wing contains deeds and debt records useful to Bellweather’s present-day disputes.

entries.name: What Happens
entries: Perrin requests originals relating to Cardon holdings. Council clerks want all civic records retained publicly. Scholars want conservation before distribution.

entries.name: NPC Behavior
entries: Perrin is especially attentive here but remains within legal procedure.

entries.name: Clues and Discoveries
entries: Several records show how emergency powers during Bellweather’s fall transferred public assets into private hands.

entries.name: Consequences
entries: Who controls these records affects later property disputes and Perrin’s political leverage.

entries.name: Scene 6: Return and Publication
entries: The party must decide who receives originals, copies, and public access.

entries.name: What Happens
entries: At minimum, the Tyren material can be copied before any ownership dispute is settled.
Brakkus urges making dangerous historical information available to more than one institution.

entries.name: Clues and Discoveries
entries: Essential revelation: Tyren is a possessing intelligence linked to the Radiant Well.

entries.name: Consequences
entries: Do not level from the library alone. Resolve the associated Bellweather property-case beat, then advance the party to level 7 and move toward Paden Square.

entries.name: Bellweather Return: One Property Case
entries: After the library is secure, resolve one Mansion-district property dispute as part of the return to Bellweather rather than scheduling a separate mandatory adventure. This beat should take about 20–45 minutes unless the players choose to pursue it further.

{@b Choose one case.} Use whichever best fits current consequences: an occupied inherited house where current residents need relocation; a forged private claim contradicted by the recovered archive; or a family vault whose codicil transferred part of the estate to a public hospice.

{@b Resolution.} Evidence from Marren Library is enough to prevent the case from hinging on one roll. The party can advocate, negotiate compensation, expose fraud, or push the Council toward a precedent. Combat occurs only if the players deliberately enter a dangerous property and the existing case material calls for it.

{@b Perrin consequence.} Perrin cites the resulting precedent publicly and selectively. He is elevated to chair the Reclamation and Emergency Works Committee because he now has money, administrative credibility, and a record of supporting reclamation. This remains a legitimate appointment, not a secret coup.
{@b Milestone.} Once Marren Library and this Bellweather property-case beat are resolved, advance the party to level 7.

entries.name: Transition to Paden Square
entries: The recovered archive and the property precedent sharpen Bellweather's understanding of who is profiting from reclamation. Intelligence from merchants and intercepted correspondence points next to Paden Square, where Tyren's network is buying material through supposedly neutral trade channels.

entries.name: Rewards
entries: {@b Treasure and rewards.} The recovery and preservation effort provides about {@b 2,400 gp} of total economic value: {@b 1,400 gp} in Council/scholarly payment and up to {@b 1,000 gp} in manuscripts, inks, and rare texts if sold. Keeping the manuscripts instead can create greater leverage with scholars and the Council. Also award 3 useful spell scrolls of levels 2–4 and one uncommon/rare utility item (default {@b Eyes of Minute Seeing}).

entries.name: Rewards
entries: These rewards are party totals for the campaign's four-character party.

items: {@b Economic value.} About 2,400 gp total: 1,400 gp in Council/scholarly payment and up to 1,000 gp in manuscripts, inks, and rare texts if sold. Keeping the manuscripts converts much of that value into scholarly and political leverage.
{@b Consumables.} 2–4 useful spell scrolls appropriate to the party's level.
{@b Permanent magic.} 1 utility-focused uncommon item, or a rare utility item only if the party is behind the campaign's permanent-item curve.
{@b Story reward.} Control over how the recovered archive is copied, published, and distributed, plus durable evidence about Tyren and the Radiant Well.

data.name: Interlude: The Mansions (Optional Reference)

entries.name: Crown-Era Adaptation Notice — Unplayed Material
entries: This chapter retains usable locations, DM maps, NPCs, clues, encounter elements, and reward ideas from the pre-Crown reclamation outline. It has NOT yet been reconciled with the Council's completed sale of Bellweather to the Crown.

Any proposed Council contract, Council payment, Council authority, Perrin promotion to Council leadership, fixed plot sequence, or automatic level advancement written below is provisional, not current campaign canon. Choose a credible sponsor and political state when the party reaches this site; do not invent a restored Council or a predetermined royal overthrow.
Appendix I governs established facts. Preserve independent motives and genuine alternatives; do not treat the former outline as a script.
{@b Recommended level:} 6–7 (optional)

entries.name: Chapter Overview
entries: {@b Purpose.} This section is a menu of property cases for use during Bellweather return scenes. It is no longer a mandatory standalone adventure.
Run one case after Marren Library as part of the level-6-to-7 arc. Keep the remaining cases available only if the players choose to investigate property disputes or Perrin's committee work further.

{@b Campaign function.} The cases establish precedents Perrin later cites, show that reclamation creates winners and losers, and give the party meaningful influence over Bellweather without adding another required multi-session dungeon.

entries.name: Running the Chapter
entries: {@b Use at the table.} Pick one featured case that matches current play. Start with the claimant, current occupants, and the disputed evidence already visible; do not require the party to clear an entire district.
{@b Time budget.} Default to 20–45 minutes. Only expand into exploration or combat if the players actively pursue the dangerous property.

{@b Evidence rule.} The decisive document or witness is recoverable automatically through reasonable investigation. Checks reveal it faster, expose additional fraud, or improve leverage; they never gate the case.
{@b Perrin.} Perrin argues for predictable ownership rules and uses whatever precedent the party creates. He can be reasonable while still accumulating procedural power.
{@b No milestone.} This interlude does not award a separate level. The Marren/property arc advances the party to level 7.

{@b Pacing valve.} If the session is already full, resolve the case with a hearing and one meaningful choice. If the players become invested, use the existing mansion maps, guardians, and hazards as optional follow-up material.

entries.name: Location and Background Details
entries: The Mansion District was once home to Bellweather's richest families. Decades of abandonment, occupation, looting, and fire have left most properties damaged, but old vaults, legal records, heirlooms, and sealed rooms make the district newly valuable as reclamation reaches the river.

The Council has no single military objective here. Instead, the party receives competing commissions from descendants, current residents, investors, neighborhood advocates, and civic officials. The point of the chapter is not to clear every mansion. Run {@b three featured property cases}, each presenting a different question about ownership.

entries.name: Featured Case A — The Vell House
entries: {@b Claim.} Mara Vell, a descendant with credible records, wants family portraits and a sealed deed box recovered.
{@b Complication.} Two families have been living in the service wing for six years and have repaired part of the property.
{@b Opposition.} 2 {@b Gargoyles} and 2 {@b Animated Armors} remain bound to the old house.
{@b Choice.} Recover the heirlooms without displacing the residents; negotiate a tenancy; or turn the entire claim over to a Council hearing.

entries.name: Featured Case B — The Doran Vault
entries: {@b Claim.} Two distant heirs present conflicting documents.
{@b Complication.} A professional recovery crew led by a {@creature Veteran|XMM} has already entered under a private contract.
{@b Opposition.} A {@creature Mimic|XMM}, unstable floors, and the rival crew if negotiations fail.

{@b Evidence.} The vault contains a notarized codicil showing that part of the estate was gifted to a public hospice before Bellweather fell. This evidence is found automatically if the vault is opened.

entries.name: Featured Case C — The Harroway Garden
entries: {@b Claim.} An investor wants the property cleared for redevelopment.
{@b Complication.} A small community of squatters has converted the surviving courtyard into homes and workshops.
{@b Opposition.} A territorial {@creature Shambling Mound|XMM} in the overgrown conservatory is the actual danger. The residents are not enemies.
{@b Choice.} Clear only the monster and leave the civic dispute to negotiation, support the investor's claim, or advocate for a new use agreement.

entries.name: Resolution
entries: The chapter is complete after the party resolves three substantial property cases or otherwise establishes a precedent that changes how Bellweather handles reclaimed estates. Their choices determine which factions gain reputation and how later residents talk about the party.

entries.name: Structure of the Chapter
entries: Run the Mansion District as three separate cases. Each mixes physical danger with a property dispute. The party can resolve them in any order.

entries.name: Case A: The Vell House
entries: A legitimate heir, Sera Vell, asks the party to clear her family home, which is occupied by dangerous creatures and a caretaker family that has lived there for years.

entries.name: What Happens
entries: Clear the unsafe upper floor, then determine what happens to the caretakers.
Sera has valid title and is not cruel; the caretakers have nowhere else to go.

entries.name: NPC Behavior
entries: Sera, a human woman, wants her home back but agrees to reasonable relocation terms. The caretaker, Old Ren, an elderly dwarf, distrusts promises made by officials.

entries.name: Encounter
entries: Use 2 {@creature Ettercap|XMM|Ettercaps} and 3 {@creature Giant Spider|XMM|Giant Spiders} in the sealed upper rooms.

entries.name: Clues and Discoveries
entries: The house records show the Vells paid city taxes even after evacuation, strengthening the legal claim.

entries.name: Consequences
entries: A negotiated tenancy or relocation earns goodwill from both sides. Immediate eviction helps strict property advocates but harms residents.

entries.name: Case B: The Doran Vault
entries: A wealthy claimant named Joric Doran presents documents claiming a sealed townhouse and its vault.

entries.name: What Happens
entries: The deed is convincing at first glance. Inside, the party encounters traps and an old household guardian.
A careful search reveals the claim papers are altered copies.

entries.name: NPC Behavior
entries: Joric is charming, impatient, and offers the party a private bonus to “avoid delays.”

entries.name: Encounter
entries: Use 1 {@creature Helmed Horror|XMM} as the old vault guardian. It attacks anyone lacking the original family signet.

entries.name: Clues and Discoveries
entries: The true deed names a different family whose surviving descendants are poor laborers in Bellweather. DC 14 Intelligence (Investigation) spots inconsistencies in Joric’s papers even before the original is found.

entries.name: Consequences
entries: Exposing the fraud embarrasses several officials who endorsed Joric. Accepting his claim gives Perrin ammunition to argue that private verification should replace public review.

entries.name: Case C: Harroway Garden
entries: A once-grand estate is now home to dozens of squatters and a productive community garden.

entries.name: What Happens
entries: The danger comes from a buried cistern contaminated by an {@creature Otyugh|XMM}. Clearing it makes the property far more valuable.
Afterward, investors offer to buy the claim from a distant heir who has never visited Bellweather.

entries.name: NPC Behavior
entries: Community leader Nessa Harroway, a half-orc woman, is not related to the old owners; she took the name from the district. She wants legal recognition for current residents.

entries.name: Encounter
entries: 1 {@creature Otyugh|XMM}. The fight takes place around narrow cistern walkways; falling into the sewage imposes the Poisoned condition until the creature takes a short rest and washes.

entries.name: Clues and Discoveries
entries: The old estate records contain no surviving direct heir, only a chain of speculative claims.

entries.name: Consequences
entries: Supporting current occupants creates a precedent for use-based claims. Supporting investors creates a precedent favoring documented ownership and capital.

entries.name: District Resolution
entries: Once all three cases are resolved, the Council debates what precedents they establish.

entries.name: What Happens
entries: Perrin argues for predictable ownership rules. Bishop Brann argues that reclamation should not create homelessness. Wern, a dwarf, cares mainly that disputes do not destabilize security.

entries.name: NPC Behavior
entries: Perrin cites the party’s own decisions selectively, whichever ones support his position.

entries.name: Consequences
entries: These legal precedents matter later when Perrin uses institutional authority against the characters.

entries.name: Transition to Chapter 11
entries: Whether the party resolves one case or several, Paden Square remains the next mandatory adventure. The Mansion cases stay available as Bellweather side material.

entries.name: Rewards
entries: {@b Treasure and rewards.} Across the chapter, keep direct payments, lawful salvage, restitution, and saleable art near {@b 2,500 gp total}; do not pay the maximum separately for every case without regard to that chapter cap. A typical resolved case is worth 600–900 gp in cash, valuables, or equivalent favor. Limit the chapter to one rare item total, default {@b Ring of Protection} from a voluntarily surrendered heirloom claim only if the party resolves the public-use dispute fairly; otherwise replace the item with 750 gp in art/coin within the same chapter budget.

entries.name: Rewards
entries: These rewards are party totals for the campaign's four-character party.

items: {@b Spendable wealth.} 1,000–1,500 gp total in portable coin, art, jewelry, and salvage.
{@b Consumables.} 2 useful consumables.
{@b Permanent magic.} 1 rare permanent item. Add an uncommon item only if the party missed earlier major rewards.
{@b Story reward.} Property claims, allies, and additional political pressure on Cardon interests.

data.name: Chapter 11: Paden Square

entries.name: Crown-Era Adaptation Notice — Unplayed Material
entries: This chapter retains usable locations, DM maps, NPCs, clues, encounter elements, and reward ideas from the pre-Crown reclamation outline. It has NOT yet been reconciled with the Council's completed sale of Bellweather to the Crown.

Any proposed Council contract, Council payment, Council authority, Perrin promotion to Council leadership, fixed plot sequence, or automatic level advancement written below is provisional, not current campaign canon. Choose a credible sponsor and political state when the party reaches this site; do not invent a restored Council or a predetermined royal overthrow.
Appendix I governs established facts. Preserve independent motives and genuine alternatives; do not treat the former outline as a script.
{@b Recommended level:} 7

entries.name: Maps
entries: {@link Player Map|https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sefjoe/no-cause-for-alarm-5etools/main/img/player/paden_square.webp}
{@link DM Keyed Map|https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sefjoe/no-cause-for-alarm-5etools/main/img/dm/paden_square.webp}

entries.name: Chapter Overview
entries: {@b Chapter purpose.} Infiltrate or turn Paden Square, identify Tyren’s agents, and prove Tyren coordinates trade as well as military force.
Scouts learn that Paden Square has become a functioning market inside occupied territory and that representatives of several hostile factions trade there.
The recovered correspondence proves that Bellweather is facing an organized strategic enemy rather than unrelated gangs.
{@b Leads onward.} The party is asked to lead the operation against Storen Gate before the enemy can reinforce it.

entries.name: Running the Chapter
entries: {@b Primary objectives.} Control exits, protect civilians, seize command correspondence, or convince part of the force to defect.
{@b Player agency.} Direct assault, infiltration, staged trade, sabotage, or faction negotiation.
{@b Fail forward.} Command evidence is not lost because one courier escapes; another source remains.

{@b Rest and pressure.} Safe long rests are available back at Ledger House. Inside the active adventure site, resting gives opposing factions time to reposition unless the characters secure a defensible refuge.

entries.name: No Cause for Alarm Beat
entries: After the party brings back evidence that supposedly separate hostile groups are coordinating, an official Council statement describes the activity as {@b "localized resistance"} and says there is {@b "no cause for alarm within Reclaimed Bellweather."} The statement may be technically true—the walls are still holding—but it minimizes what the characters have actually learned.
If the party brings the notice to Ledger House, Brakkus can read the final sentence and reply, {@b "Well. That settles it, then."} He immediately starts checking the shutters and cellar stores.

entries.name: Encounter Guidance
entries: Paden Square is primarily an infiltration, observation, and escape problem. Use the finite security roster exactly as written; difficulty comes from Suspicion, the courier's movement, civilians, and competing objectives rather than extra guards or inflated hit points.

entries.name: Table-Ready Session Package
entries: {@b Milestone.} The party enters Paden Square at level 7 and remains level 7 afterward; completing the Paden Square + Storen Gate arc advances the party to level 8.

{@b Required objectives.} Complete any 2 of 3: identify Tyren's courier, learn what the network is purchasing, and secure the command correspondence or auctioned material. Completing all 3 improves the Storen Gate briefing but is not required.

{@b Finite security.} Market security consists of 1 {@creature Veteran|XMM}, 4 {@creature Thug|XMM|Thugs}, and 2 {@creature Scout|XMM|Scouts}. Tyren's courier uses a {@creature Spy|XMM} stat block and tries to escape rather than fight. Civilians flee if violence begins. No additional combatants appear from the crowd.

{@b Suspicion 0–3.} Start at 0. A conspicuous failed deception, obvious theft attempt, or visible snooping increases Suspicion by 1. At 1, a Scout shadows the party. At 2, Balden personally questions them and the courier becomes cautious. At 3, security orders them out and the courier leaves with the correspondence; this creates an escape/chase scene rather than an automatic mass combat.

{@b Cover.} A plausible story plus appropriate behavior requires no roll. When a lie is actually tested, use DC 14 Deception. A real sponsor, captured invitation, or useful merchant contact grants advantage.

{@b Auction.} Run three lots. The target material appears in lot 3. During each lot the party gets one meaningful action to observe, bid, lift a document, contact the courier, or manipulate security. The courier departs immediately after lot 3 if Suspicion is 2 or higher.

{@b Securing the correspondence.} DC 15 Sleight of Hand steals it unnoticed; DC 15 Deception or Persuasion can create a handoff or private meeting when fiction supports it; defeating or cornering the courier also works. Failure raises Suspicion rather than erasing the clue.

{@b Short rest.} Paden Square is not a safe place to spend an hour once the auction is underway. If the party leaves to Short Rest, the auction resolves and the courier departs, but the broker or a tail can still point them toward an escape route or Storen Gate contact.

{@b Escape procedure.} If needed, require 3 successes before 2 failures using Athletics, Acrobatics, Stealth, Deception, or a clearly useful spell, normally DC 14. On success the party exits cleanly. On failure, surviving security catches them at the last exit for one final confrontation or forces them to abandon one nonessential piece of evidence.
{@b Pacing valve.} If time is short, Garin identifies the courier after one good conversation and move directly to lot 3. If time remains, play all three lots and let Suspicion build naturally.

entries.name: Courier Clock
entries: The courier begins near the auction floor with the correspondence. Once Suspicion reaches 2 or combat begins, start a 3-round escape clock.
{@b Round 1.} The courier moves toward a prepared side exit while one Scout shadows or screens the route.
{@b Round 2.} The courier reaches the exit unless physically blocked, deceived into stopping, restrained, or forced onto another route.

{@b Round 3.} The courier disappears into the hostile district. The party can still recover the essential intelligence through Garin, auction records, or a captured security member, but loses the cleanest direct evidence.
A clever spell, blocked route, forged instruction, or social play can stop the courier without a check when it plainly works. Do not turn the clock into mandatory Athletics rolls.

entries.name: Security Deployment
entries: If violence begins, 1 {@creature Veteran|XMM} and 2 {@creature Thug|XMM|Thugs} hold the auction floor and protect civilian evacuation routes. The other 2 Thugs move to block the nearest party exit. The 2 {@creature Scout|XMM|Scouts} use elevated cover and track the courier's route.

Security is trying to end the disturbance and protect the market, not fight to the death. The Veteran calls for withdrawal or terms if reduced below half hit points and at least 3 other security members are down.
If the party drops the first defenders quickly, surviving security disengages toward exits and cover instead of feeding themselves into the party one at a time.

entries.name: Expected Session Shape
entries: Mission, cover, and entering the square: about 20–30 minutes.
Market contacts and Suspicion-building play: about 35–50 minutes.
Three-lot auction: about 30–45 minutes.
Courier confrontation, negotiation, or security fight: about 40–60 minutes.
Escape and Bellweather debrief: about 20–30 minutes.

{@b Keyed-area encounters.} When a scene and a keyed location describe the same encounter, use the roster and objective in the scene. Creatures listed only in the keyed reference apply when the characters explore that location outside the scene sequence.

entries.name: Location and Background Details
entries: Paden Square was once Bellweather's commercial heart and remains a trading nexus inside occupied territory. The Council learns that a supposedly powerful magic item will be auctioned there and that Tyren may send a representative.

entries.name: Entering the Square
entries: Paden Square is busy, commercially active, and occupied by people from many factions and species. The party can enter as merchants, hired guards, couriers, bidders, entertainers, laborers, or invited guests. Cover depends on credentials and behavior, not ancestry.

If the characters' cover is weak, use a group Charisma (Deception) check against DC 14. On a failure, security questions them, demands a sponsor, or escorts them away; combat is only one possible consequence.

entries.name: Security and Scale
entries: The square is too crowded and fortified for a sensible direct assault, but do not represent that with hundreds of combatants. A frontal attack triggers escalating security, civilian panic, blocked exits, and a clear need to withdraw. Use one immediate security encounter and then a chase or escape procedure.

entries.name: Scene 1: Mission and Cover
entries: Paden Square is an active market inside hostile territory. The objective is intelligence, not extermination.

entries.name: What Happens
entries: The party can enter disguised as buyers, escort a cooperating merchant, sneak across rooftops, or stage a diversion.
Their goals are to identify who enforces the truce, learn what Tyren's network is purchasing, and seize correspondence if possible.

entries.name: Clues and Discoveries
entries: Bellweather knows representatives of several hostile factions attend the same market without fighting.

entries.name: Consequences
entries: A violent entrance causes vendors and couriers to scatter, making intelligence harder to recover.

entries.name: Scene 2: The Market
entries: Run the square as a social environment before combat.

entries.name: What Happens
entries: Merchants sell weapons, food, medicine, stolen civic goods, and information. Many are criminals, but some are ordinary people trading because official routes are closed.
The party can gather three pieces of intelligence through conversation, observation, bribery, or theft.

entries.name: NPC Behavior
entries: Garin, a goblin broker, is talkative and self-protective. Balden, a human enforcer, speaks for the market’s security committee. Neither is automatically hostile.

{@b NPC description — Garin and Balden.} Garin is a small, neatly dressed goblin man of indeterminate middle age with ink-stained fingertips, bright rings, and the constant half-smile of a broker who expects every conversation to become a transaction. Balden is a tall, heavyset human man in his thirties, shaved-headed and watchful in reinforced street clothes, standing just far enough back to let Garin do the talking until trouble begins.

entries.name: Clues and Discoveries
entries: The “Boss” buys maps, old records, alchemical reagents, and captives with unusual magical exposure.
Couriers use the crossed-line mark and carry sealed packets toward Storen Gate.
The market truce is enforced by threats from a central command, not mutual trust.

entries.name: Consequences
entries: Good social play can complete most objectives without combat.

entries.name: Scene 3: The Auction
entries: A private auction offers an old civic map, captured correspondence, and a magical research folio.

entries.name: What Happens
entries: The party can bid, steal, expose a seller, or disrupt the auction.
If they win or seize the correspondence, it names Storen Gate as the primary logistics route.

entries.name: NPC Behavior
entries: Garin will quietly help the party if convinced Bellweather can keep the market open under safer rules later.

entries.name: Encounter
entries: If combat starts, use 1 {@creature Veteran|XMM}, 4 {@creature Thug|XMM|Thugs}, and 2 {@creature Scout|XMM|Scouts}. Civilians flee rather than fight.

entries.name: Clues and Discoveries
entries: The correspondence refers to the central commander only as “Boss,” but includes orders to move forces through Storen Gate and references “the host” in singular terms.

entries.name: Consequences
entries: Capturing documents is more important than defeating every enemy.

entries.name: Scene 4: Escape or Negotiated Exit
entries: Once the party’s purpose is exposed, exits begin to close.

entries.name: What Happens
entries: They can escape through alleys, bargain with Garin, create a crowd panic, or fight a delaying action.
Use a three-success chase if needed: Athletics, Acrobatics, Stealth, Deception, or clever magic.

entries.name: Clues and Discoveries
entries: A captured courier can confirm that orders ultimately come from Varen Keep.

entries.name: Consequences
entries: If the party is captured, market leaders prefer ransom or trade to execution; allies can create a second chance.

entries.name: Scene 5: Bellweather Learns the Scale
entries: The evidence proves the hostile network has logistics, markets, couriers, and strategic command.

entries.name: What Happens
entries: Wern proposes taking Storen Gate to cut the supply route. Perrin supports the plan because it would open valuable interior districts.

entries.name: Consequences
entries: Do not level here. The party remains level 7; securing Storen Gate completes the Paden + Storen arc and advances the party to level 8.

entries.name: Transition to Chapter 12
entries: The party is asked to lead the operation against Storen Gate before the enemy can reinforce it.

entries.name: Rewards
entries: {@b Rewards.} The Council pays {@b 2,000 gp} for reliable intelligence on the command network and another {@b 2,000 gp} if the party secures the auctioned material for civic custody, for a maximum cash reward of {@b 4,000 gp}. Material sold back to lawful owners should create favors or restitution rather than duplicate the payout.

entries.name: Rewards
entries: These rewards are party totals for the campaign's four-character party.

items: {@b Spendable wealth.} About 1,000 gp in seized payroll, trade goods, and bounty or reward money.
{@b Consumables.} 2–3 useful consumables.
{@b Permanent magic.} 1 rare permanent item or equivalent party-use item.
{@b Story reward.} Disruption of the hostile intelligence network and improved access toward Storen Gate.

data.name: Chapter 12: Storen Gate

Any proposed Council contract, Council payment, Council authority, Perrin promotion to Council leadership, fixed plot sequence, or automatic level advancement written below is provisional, not current campaign canon. Choose a credible sponsor and political state when the party reaches this site; do not invent a restored Council or a predetermined royal overthrow.
Appendix I governs established facts. Preserve independent motives and genuine alternatives; do not treat the former outline as a script.
{@b Recommended level:} 7

entries.name: Maps
entries: {@link Player Map|https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sefjoe/no-cause-for-alarm-5etools/main/img/player/storen_gate.webp}
{@link DM Keyed Map|https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sefjoe/no-cause-for-alarm-5etools/main/img/dm/storen_gate.webp}

entries.name: Chapter Overview
entries: {@b Chapter purpose.} Take Storen Gate as a strategic objective and open the safest land route into deeper ruins.
Storen Gate blocks the safest land route into the deeper ruins and allows Tyren-aligned forces to move troops without interference.
Capturing Storen Gate opens the city’s deeper districts and shifts the campaign from local reclamation to open strategic conflict.
{@b Leads onward.} With the gate open, reports from Valen Cemetery become urgent: missing residents, opened graves, and organized undead movement.

entries.name: Running the Chapter
entries: {@b Primary objectives.} Open/hold the gate, prevent a signal, defeat or turn the command element.
{@b Player agency.} Climb, infiltrate, bribe an insider, create a diversion, or conduct a frontal attack.
{@b Fail forward.} Failure to stop a signal adds reinforcements or pressure rather than ending the scenario.

{@b Rest and pressure.} Safe long rests are available back at Ledger House. Inside the active adventure site, resting gives opposing factions time to reposition unless the characters secure a defensible refuge.

entries.name: Encounter Guidance
entries: Treat this as a military objective. Success is measured by controlling the alarm, gate mechanism, command post, and reinforcement timing rather than by defeating every defender.

entries.name: Table-Ready Session Package
entries: {@b Milestone.} The party enters Storen Gate at level 7. Securing the gate completes the Paden + Storen arc and advances the party to level 8.

{@b Four objectives.} Silence the alarm, open the gate, seize or turn the command post, and hold the mechanism until Bellweather troops establish control. The party can approach these in any order that makes sense.

{@b Finite defenders.} Wall: 4 {@creature Scout|XMM|Scouts} and 2 {@creature Guard|XMM|Guards}. Gate mechanism: 1 {@creature Veteran|XMM} and 4 Guards. Command post: 1 {@creature Hobgoblin Captain|XMM} and 3 {@creature Hobgoblin Warrior|XMM|Hobgoblin Warriors}. Alarm reinforcement: 1 Veteran and 4 Guards drawn from the same garrison reserve. No further waves appear.

{@b Alarm.} If the bell rings, the reserve reaches the gate mechanism at the end of round 2. Silencing the bell before then cancels the reserve. A failed stealth or deception attempt can start questioning without automatically ringing the alarm.

{@b Gate mechanism.} Removing the locking bar requires DC 15 Athletics or two uninterrupted actions with suitable tools. Once the bar is removed, opening the gate takes one action. Bellweather troops enter at the start of the next round and secure ordinary rank-and-file fighting off-map.

{@b Command morale.} The captain tries to destroy orders and retreat if the gate opens before the command post is secured. The Hobgoblins surrender or withdraw when the captain falls and Bellweather troops control the gate.

{@b Hold sequence.} After the gate opens, run at most 4 rounds of pressure: round 1 missile fire from surviving sentries; round 2 fire or sabotage at the mechanism; round 3 a retreating squad attempts to rebar the gate; round 4 the command element makes its final push or withdraws. Use surviving listed defenders rather than spawning new enemies.

{@b Useful DCs.} Forge or bluff a routine inspection DC 14 Deception; jam the bell DC 13 Sleight of Hand or appropriate tools; remove the gate bar DC 15 Athletics; stop fire at the mechanism DC 14 Survival, Arcana, or an appropriate spell; identify the commander's escape route DC 14 Investigation.

{@b Short rest.} Before the gate is open, a Short Rest gives defenders time to consolidate, burn secondary orders, and place the reserve at the gate. After Bellweather troops enter and the command post is secure, a Short Rest is safe.

{@b Fail-forward.} If the alarm sounds or the commander escapes, the gate can still be taken. The cost is an extra reserve fight, lost secondary intelligence, or the commander becoming a later complication—not mission failure.
{@b Pacing valve.} If time is short, Bellweather scouts provide a route directly to either the alarm tower or gate mechanism. If time remains, run the full four-objective assault.

entries.name: Two-Phase Assault
entries: {@b Phase 1 — Wall and Gate.} Treat the wall and gate mechanism as one connected tactical problem, not two mandatory combats. If fighting begins on the wall, surviving wall defenders fall back toward the gate mechanism. Roll a new initiative only if there is a real break in the action.

{@b Phase 2 — Command and Hold.} Once the gate is opening, the command element either makes its move or attempts to withdraw with the orders. The hold sequence happens inside this same phase using surviving listed defenders.
This keeps the assault to at most two full combats while preserving the feeling of taking a fortified gate.

entries.name: Objective Payoffs
entries: {@b Silence the alarm.} The 1 Veteran + 4 Guard reserve never deploys.
{@b Open the gate.} Bellweather troops arrive at the start of the next round and remove ordinary rank-and-file fighting from the encounter.
{@b Secure the command post.} The orders survive, the commander cannot organize the round-4 push, and remaining Hobgoblins lose coordinated retreat.

{@b Hold the mechanism.} If the alarm is silent and command is already secured, Bellweather establishes control after 2 hold rounds instead of 4. If either remains unresolved, use the full 4-round hold sequence.
Player success should shorten and simplify the battle. Do not make them complete four rounds merely because the chapter says 'hold' if they have already solved the reasons the gate is threatened.

entries.name: Defender Movement
entries: Wall survivors retreat toward the gate mechanism when half their group is defeated or the alarm has been rung.
The gate Veteran prioritizes keeping a character away from the locking bar; Guards shove, grapple, block lanes, or use Help when that is more useful than dealing a few points of damage.

The Hobgoblin Captain tries to preserve the orders until the gate opens. Once Bellweather troops are entering, the Captain either burns the secondary papers and retreats or commits to one final push if an exit remains.
The reserve, if activated, arrives once at the end of round 2. There is no second reserve.

entries.name: Expected Session Shape
entries: Planning and choosing an approach: about 20–30 minutes.
Wall/gate infiltration or Phase 1 combat: about 45–70 minutes.
Opening the mechanism and Bellweather entry: about 15–25 minutes.
Command confrontation plus hold sequence: about 60–75 minutes.
Orders, surrender, and aftermath: about 15–20 minutes.

{@b Keyed-area encounters.} When a scene and a keyed location describe the same encounter, use the roster and objective in the scene. Creatures listed only in the keyed reference apply when the characters explore that location outside the scene sequence.

entries.name: Perrin's Rise: Emergency Authority
entries: Opening Storen Gate turns reclamation into a larger security and trade problem. Perrin's committee authority expands into emergency contracting, public notices, and coordination with merchants and guards. He is now the Council's dominant administrative voice even when other councilors disagree with him.
Wern still controls military judgment and Bishop Brann still carries moral/public influence; Perrin's power comes from procedure, money, records, and the ability to make government move.

entries.name: The Wall
entries: Characters approaching openly are warned away from the wall and directed to the gate. Characters climbing, flying, or sneaking across contend with watch rotations, cover, and magical observation. Resolve the approach with the normal 2024 stealth, perception, and spell rules rather than percentage detection.

entries.name: The Gate
entries: Merchant wagons still pass through under permit, which gives the party several options:

items: buy or borrow a legitimate wagon and paperwork;
forge a permit or impersonate a supply crew;
hide among cargo and make a group Dexterity (Stealth) check against the guards' passive Perception;
bribe a corrupt clerk;
create a distraction elsewhere on the wall;
attack directly.

entries: Failure does not mean instant combat. Guards question the party, demand inspection, separate one character for verification, or call an officer. Combat begins only if the situation escalates there.

entries.name: Capturing the Gate
entries: The gate can be secured by defeating the command group, convincing enough troops to stand down, or disabling the portcullis and signal system long enough for Bellweather's forces to arrive. Once the defenders' command collapses, rank-and-file troops may retreat or surrender.

entries.name: Scene 1: Planning the Assault
entries: Storen Gate is a military objective with four goals: silence the alarm, open the gate, seize the command post, and hold it.

entries.name: What Happens
entries: The party can choose stealth, climbing, sabotage, infiltration with captured signals, or direct assault.
Bellweather troops wait out of sight until the gate opens or a signal is given.

entries.name: Clues and Discoveries
entries: Scouts identify the alarm tower, gate mechanism, barracks, and command post on the keyed map.

entries.name: Consequences
entries: Each objective completed before open combat creates its specific payoff in the Table-Ready Session Package; only silencing the alarm removes the reserve.

entries.name: Scene 2: The Wall
entries: Sentries control the outer wall and alarm bell.

entries.name: What Happens
entries: If the bell rings, the single listed reserve of 1 {@creature Veteran|XMM} and 4 {@creature Guard|XMM|Guards} reaches the gate mechanism at the end of round 2.
Cutting the bell rope, jamming the clapper, or silently removing the sentries prevents the reinforcement.

entries.name: Encounter
entries: 4 {@creature Scout|XMM|Scouts}, 2 {@creature Guard|XMM|Guards}.

entries.name: Clues and Discoveries
entries: A signal chart shows Paden Square, Storen Gate, and Varen Keep on the same command network.

entries.name: Consequences
entries: Silencing the alarm gives the party control over the pace of the assault.

entries.name: Scene 3: Gate Mechanism
entries: The mechanism room is defended because the enemy expects Bellweather to want the gate intact.

entries.name: What Happens
entries: A character at the controls can open the gate with an action after the locking bar is removed. Removing it requires DC 15 Strength (Athletics) or two uninterrupted actions with tools.

entries.name: Encounter
entries: 1 {@creature Veteran|XMM}, 4 {@creature Guard|XMM|Guards}.

entries.name: Consequences
entries: Opening the gate brings Bellweather troops into the battle at the start of the next round.

entries.name: Scene 4: Command Post
entries: The local commander tries to destroy orders and retreat toward the inner city.

entries.name: What Happens
entries: Stop the commander, seize documents, or pursue if necessary.

entries.name: NPC Behavior
entries: {@creature Commander Vesk|NCFA} uses the Hobgoblin Captain stat block and values survival over martyrdom.

entries.name: Encounter
entries: 1 {@creature Hobgoblin Captain|XMM}, 3 {@creature Hobgoblin Warrior|XMM|Hobgoblin Warriors}.

entries.name: Clues and Discoveries
entries: Orders refer to Tyren directly for the first time in contemporary documents and instruct commanders to “protect the host.”

entries.name: Consequences
entries: A living Vesk can confirm Tyren is not physically present at every command site.

entries.name: Scene 5: Hold the Gate
entries: The party must hold the command position until Bellweather forces secure both approaches.

entries.name: What Happens
entries: Run 2 hold rounds if the alarm is silent and the command post is already secured; otherwise run up to 4. Present one threat each round using surviving listed defenders: missile fire, sabotage near the mechanism, an attempt to rebar the gate, or the command element's final push. Do not create new squads for the hold sequence.

entries.name: Encounter
entries: Use small groups of {@creature Hobgoblin Warrior|XMM|Hobgoblin Warriors} or {@creature Guard|XMM|Guards}; do not place dozens of creatures on the map.

entries.name: Consequences
entries: Success opens the deeper city and marks the transition from reclamation to open war.

entries.name: Transition to Chapter 13
entries: With the gate open, reports from Valen Cemetery become urgent: missing residents, opened graves, and organized undead movement.

entries.name: Rewards
entries: {@b Rewards.} The Council pays {@b 5,000 gp total} for opening and holding Storen Gate, reflecting the strategic importance of the objective. Captured military supplies become Council property rather than additional resale loot. Also provide one rare consumable or utility reward (default {@b Potion of Speed}).

entries.name: Rewards
entries: These rewards are party totals for the campaign's four-character party.

items: {@b Spendable wealth.} 1,250–1,750 gp in Council military reward and captured command valuables.
{@b Consumables.} 3 useful consumables.
{@b Permanent magic.} 1 rare permanent item from the command post or armory.
{@b Story reward.} Gate access, garrison support, and reopening of a major trade route.
